stories.title: مولانا فضل الرحمان کا حراست میں ہونے کا دعویٰ، پولیس کی تردید
stories.summary:
جمعیت علمائے اسلام (جے یو آئی) کے سربراہ مولانا فضل الرحمان نے لاہور میں ایک اجتماع سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے دعویٰ کیا کہ پولیس نے انھیں گرفتار کر لیا ہے اور وہ اب ان کی حراست میں ہیں۔ تاہم، لاہور پولیس کے کیپیٹل سٹی پولیس آفیسر (سی سی پی او) بلال کمیانا نے اس دعوے کی سختی سے تردید کرتے ہوئے واضح کیا کہ پولیس نے مولانا کو حراست میں نہیں لیا کیونکہ وہ کسی مقدمے میں مطلوب نہیں تھے۔

اس واقعے کے بعد جے یو آئی نے ملک بھر میں دھرنے ختم کرنے اور جمعے کی نماز کے بعد ملک گیر احتجاجی مظاہرے کرنے کا اعلان کیا۔ خیبر پختونخوا کے ضلعی ہیڈ کوارٹرز میں بھی احتجاجی مظاہروں کی تیاریاں کی گئیں، جبکہ پشاور میں موٹروے ٹول پلازا بند کرنے کے الزام میں چودہ افراد کی گرفتاری کی اطلاعات بھی سامنے آئیں۔

دوسری جانب، کویت میں ایک ڈرون حملے کے دوران دو اطالوی شہریوں کی ہلاکت کے بعد خطے میں کشیدگی پائی جاتی ہے۔ اٹلی کے وزیر خارجہ انتونیو تایانی نے بتایا کہ یہ شہری فضائی دفاعی نظام پر کام کر رہے تھے جب ایرانی ڈرونز نے فوجی تنصیبات کو نشانہ بنایا۔ تاہم، ایرانی وزیر خارجہ عباس عراقچی نے کویت پر ڈرون حملے میں تہران کے ملوث ہونے کی مکمل تردید کی ہے۔

ادھر، امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے مشرق وسطیٰ کی صورتحال پر گفتگو کرتے ہوئے دعویٰ کیا کہ ایران اسرائیل اور دیگر ممالک پر جوہری ہتھیار داغ سکتا تھا، اور اس خطرے سے نمٹنے کے لیے مضبوط موقف اپنانا ضروری تھا۔ اسلام آباد میں مکہ دفاعی اتحاد کی کمیٹی کے اجلاس اور سعودی عرب کے شہر جازان میں آئل ریفائنری پر پروجیکٹائل حملے کی بھی اطلاعات موصول ہوئی ہیں۔

stories.title: Indian Politician Hosts Lavish Wedding Drawing Hundreds of Thousands of Guests
stories.summary:
An extravagant wedding hosted by Indian politician Anant Singh in Bihar's Nadawan village attracted approximately 400,000 attendees, causing massive traffic gridlocks and unusual spectacles. Singh, a six-time lawmaker facing multiple criminal charges including murder, invited villagers, political allies, and VIPs to celebrate his daughter's nuptials on Wednesday. According to Singh's confidant Munna Singh, the massive crowd was served 500,000 traditional sweets and a vegetarian feast prepared by 500 chefs and cooks.

The scale of the celebration overwhelmed local infrastructure, completely halting traffic on roads leading to the venue. One politician reportedly abandoned his vehicle to ride a tractor across farm fields, while organizers constructed five helipads to accommodate VIP arrivals. Footage from the Press Trust of India showed large crowds jostling for views, with some attendees climbing trees and electricity pylons. Additionally, a planned horse race featuring 200 horses had to be postponed after roughly 100,000 spectators arrived to watch.

The festivities featured intricate floral arrangements with flowers imported from China, a large fireworks display, and luxurious transportation for the couple. The bride arrived in a luxury BMW, and the groom traveled with a convoy of approximately 200 cars. The event underscores the immense scale of the Indian wedding industry, where KPMG estimates more than 10 million weddings occur annually, generating a market worth $40 to $50 billion.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Opens Lower Amid Broad Selling Pressure
stories.summary:
Negative sentiment hit the Pakistan Stock Exchange on Friday as the benchmark KSE-100 Index dropped nearly 200 points during early trading. At 9:30 am, the index hovered at 177,895.43, marking a decline of 165.25 points or 0.09 percent. Selling pressure was observed across multiple key sectors, including automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration, and power generation.

Market analysts from Ismail Iqbal Securities anticipated ongoing volatility due to rising global oil prices, geopolitical tensions, and active rollover week trading. This downward movement followed a marginally lower close on Thursday, when cautious investor behavior and profit-taking offset selective buying, pushing the KSE-100 Index down by 60.56 points to finish at 178,060.69 points.

Globally, financial markets experienced mixed conditions as Asian shares prepared to conclude a difficult month. A holiday lull provided some relief from artificial intelligence concerns, while the US dollar maintained strength from safe-haven demand and rate hike expectations. Meanwhile, oil prices headed toward their first weekly increase in four weeks despite Brent crude futures slipping 0.4 percent to $96.14 a barrel on Friday.

stories.title: Indian Lawmaker's Massive Wedding in Bihar Draws 400,000 Attendees
stories.summary:
Anant Singh, a six-time lawmaker in India's poorest state of Bihar, hosted a wedding for his daughter on Wednesday that drew an estimated 400,000 guests. Singh, who faces numerous criminal charges including murder, invited local villagers, political allies, and VIPs to his native village of Nadawan. The massive gathering caused severe traffic disruptions, prompting one politician to abandon his car and use a tractor across farm fields to reach the venue.

To accommodate the staggering number of attendees, organizers established five helipads for VIP arrivals and enlisted a team of 500 chefs and cooks to provide a vegetarian feast alongside 500,000 traditional sweets. Footage agency Press Trust of India captured crowds jostling for views, with spectators perching on trees and electricity towers. A planned horse race involving 200 horses had to be postponed after roughly 100,000 people turned up to watch the spectacle.

The celebration also featured decorations with Chinese-imported flowers, a fireworks show, a luxury BMW for the bride, and a 200-car convoy for the groom. This event highlights the sheer magnitude of India's wedding sector, which sees over 10 million celebrations annually and is valued between $40 billion and $50 billion by KPMG.

stories.title: صرف چوبیس روپے جیب میں رکھنے والا بھارتی نوجوان کروڑ پتی بن گیا
stories.summary:
انڈیا کی ریاست مہاراشٹر سے تعلق رکھنے والے اٹھائیس سالہ بھوشن ٹھاکرے نے مشہور ٹیلی ویژن گیم شو 'کون بنے گا کروڑ پتی' (کے بی سی) میں ایک کروڑ روپے جیت لیے ہیں۔ بھوشن کا تعلق ایک انتہائی غریب مزدور خاندان سے ہے، اور وہ جب اس شو میں شرکت کے لیے ممبئی روانہ ہوئے تو ان کی جیب میں صرف چوبیس روپے موجود تھے۔

بھوشن نے سات کروڑ روپے کے سوال کا جواب دینے کے بجائے ایک کروڑ روپے کی انعامی رقم کے ساتھ کھیل چھوڑنے کا فیصلہ کیا۔ انھوں نے سنہ 2016 میں پہلی بار کے بی سی کے لیے رجسٹریشن کروائی تھی اور تقریباً ایک دہائی کی مسلسل کوششوں اور آڈیشنز کے بعد آخر کار سنہ 2026 میں وہ اس منزل تک پہنچنے میں کامیاب ہوئے۔ ان کے والد نے بچپن سے مزدوری کی ہے اور والدہ کو بھی مالی مشکلات کا سامنا رہا ہے۔

تاریخ میں ایم اے کرنے کے بعد بھوشن اس وقت پولیٹیکل سائنس میں ماسٹرز کے ساتھ یو پی ایس سی کے امتحان کی تیاری کر رہے ہیں۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ اس بڑی انعامی رقم سے ان کے خاندان کی زندگی بدل جائے گی، اور ان کی پہلی ترجیح اپنی والدہ کے لیے زیور خریدنا ہے جنھوں نے ان کی پڑھائی کے لیے اپنے زیورات فروخت کیے تھے۔

یہ کامیابی بھوشن اور ان کے پورے خاندان کے لیے ایک طویل جدوجہد اور صبر آزما سفر کا نتیجہ ہے۔ گاؤں واپسی پر ان کے استقبال کی تیاریاں کی جا رہی ہیں، اور وہ اب بہتر کوچنگ حاصل کرکے اپنے کیریئر کو مزید آگے بڑھانے کا ارادہ رکھتے ہیں۔ نوجوانوں کے نام اپنے پیغام میں ان کا کہنا ہے کہ انسان کو ہمیشہ بڑے خواب دیکھنے چاہیے اور ان کی تکمیل کے لیے ہمیشگی سے محنت کرنی چاہیے۔

stories.title: Hamas Chief Weighs Response After Israeli Strikes Kill Ten in Gaza
stories.summary:
Hamas political bureau head Khalil Al-Hayya stated on Thursday that the group could no longer endure ongoing Israeli attacks after local medics confirmed that Israeli strikes killed at least 10 people in Gaza. The casualties included Khaled Abu Nada, who served as a member of Hamas's political office and the Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education. Abu Nada was killed during the third consecutive night of air attacks when an apartment in Deir Al-Balah was struck.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu noted that Abu Nada's death was part of recent targeted killings against senior Hamas officials, with Israel having eliminated approximately 80 fighters over the past month. Abu Nada was the third senior official targeted since Tuesday, following two security officials. The Israeli military stated that Abu Nada managed Hamas's economic portfolio and banking network, asserting that his removal would hurt the group's financial capabilities.

Hamas confirmed Abu Nada's political role and condemned his death alongside other academic and civilian casualties as a violation of the Gaza ceasefire agreement and international law. Hayya stated that the group would consult other Palestinian factions regarding a potential response to daily killings and violations. Furthermore, Hamas held US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace politically and morally responsible for failing to halt the violence and providing cover for civilian attacks.

stories.title: Pakistan Struggles With Over 25 Million Out-Of-School Children Amid Constitutional Failures
stories.summary:
Pakistan is grappling with a growing crisis as the number of out-of-school children crosses 25 million, highlighting the state's failure to provide universal education despite decades of constitutional guarantees. Successive Pakistani constitutions, beginning in 1956 and 1962, alongside the 1973 Constitution's Article 37(b) and the 18th Amendment's Article 25-A in 2010, have repeatedly mandated free and compulsory primary and secondary education. However, continuous policy and governance failures have left millions of children without educational access, leading to lost human capital and intergenerational poverty. Unesco data indicates that Pakistan has a much higher proportion of out-of-school primary-age children compared to its regional neighbors, including India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, the Maldives, and Sri Lanka.

Addressing this massive educational deficit requires far more than basic enrollment campaigns; it demands a staggering expansion of infrastructure and human resources. Based on an illustrative class size of 40 students, Pakistan would need approximately 628,750 new classrooms to accommodate the excluded children. Furthermore, hiring a staffing ratio of 1.2 teachers per classroom would necessitate roughly 754,500 additional educators. Recruiting these staff members at an initial BPS-14 pay rate of Rs27,060 per month would generate an annual salary bill of roughly Rs245 billion, excluding critical costs such as allowances, pensions, teacher training, and facility construction.

The scale of this financial obligation far surpasses the country's current fiscal allocations, including the reported Rs962 billion spent on education in the 2024-25 fiscal year. Experts note that the central problem is not merely calculating the cost of educating these children, but understanding why the state has failed to establish a sustainable financing mechanism to uphold its foundational legal promises. Failing to build a functioning educational infrastructure undermines democratic institutions, economic development, and knowledge-based growth. Ultimately, analysts argue that the true metric of state success cannot rely on unfulfilled policy announcements or budgets, but must be judged by the visible presence of every child actively learning inside a classroom.

stories.title: Cricket Australia Forum on 2018 Ball-Tampering Will Not Reassign Blame
stories.summary:
Cricket Australia has clarified the terms of reference for its upcoming independent forum regarding the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa. The six-week proceeding, overseen by Australian barrister Fiona McLeod, is strictly designed as an information-gathering and listening process rather than a disciplinary review. According to official guidelines published on Friday, the forum will not determine individual responsibility, make adverse findings against any participants, or revisit penalties previously imposed by integrity units. Participation will be entirely voluntary, aimed at supporting the welfare of those impacted and offering a safe space for individuals to share their experiences without fear of retribution or disadvantage.

The forum was announced following renewed public discussion sparked by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja, who claimed that the entire team was aware of the ball-tampering plot during the South African tour. Under the original 2018 investigation, Cricket Australia found only three players culpable: then-captain Steve Smith, opening batsman David Warner, and Cameron Bancroft. Consequently, Smith and Warner received 12-month bans, while Bancroft was suspended for nine months. While players like Warner, Bancroft, and Chadd Sayers have supported Khawaja's remarks about broader team knowledge, current captain Pat Cummins alongside bowlers Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have firmly denied any prior awareness of the incident.

Despite the renewed public controversy, Cricket Australia recently reaffirmed its support for Pat Cummins to remain captain of both the test and one-day international teams. The scope of the upcoming independent sessions will evaluate ball-management practices across all four tests played during the South African tour, extending beyond the Newlands test where the scandal originally surfaced. The forum will also review the methodology and conduct of the original 2018 investigation. Cricket Australia chairman David Boon emphasized that the initiative provides the best opportunity for stakeholders to speak and be heard. Once concluded, a full report on the forum will be published, with Cricket Australia committing to a formal response within 30 days.

stories.title: India Fights Back as New Zealand Reaches 131-4 at Tea on Day One
stories.summary:
India mounted a strong comeback in the second session of the second Test against New Zealand, claiming three quick wickets to leave the home side at 131 for four at tea on day one at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. After New Zealand resumed their innings at 77 for one following lunch, having been put in to bat by India captain Shubman Gill, Indian bowlers capitalized on a grassy pitch. Pace bowler Akash Deep led the resurgence with a devastating spell, striking twice either side of another dismissal by Anshul Kamboj to dismantle the middle order and shift momentum back toward the visiting team.

New Zealand captain Tom Latham had earlier shrugged off a poor run of form to anchor the innings with a resilient 59 runs. However, his dismissal occurred early in the second session when Deep induced an edge caught behind by the wicketkeeper. In the very next over, number three batsman Henry Nicholls was caught for 16 at deep backward square leg after attempting a loose slog off Kamboj. Deep immediately returned to trap Rachin Ravindra caught behind for a duck, resulting in a dramatic collapse where New Zealand lost three wickets for no additional runs.

Earlier in the day, New Zealand's opening stand remained resilient until the final delivery of the opening session, when Devon Conway was dismissed lbw for 31 by debutant fast bowler Gurnoor Brar, marking the newcomer's maiden Test wicket. Brar represented the sole change to India's starting eleven from the drawn first Test in Wellington, replacing Prasidh Krishna. At the tea break, New Zealand number five Daryl Mitchell was batting on six alongside wicketkeeper Tom Blundell on eight runs. The match carries substantial implications for both nations as they vie for a spot in the World Test Championship final.

stories.title: China Industrial Profits Accelerate in October Amid Uneven Economic Recovery
stories.summary:
Profit growth among China's major industrial firms accelerated significantly in October, marking the fastest pace in five months. Data released by the National Bureau of Statistics on Friday revealed that industrial profits rose 20.1% year-on-year last month, improving upon the 14.4% gain recorded in September. For the first ten months of the year, cumulative profits climbed 16%, quickening from the 15.5% increase observed during the January-September period. These figures serve as a critical gauge of corporate health, investment sentiment, and the overall impact of Beijing's recent economic stimulus policies.

Despite the headline acceleration, analysts highlighted a widening structural divergence across different industrial sectors. Driven heavily by external demand and high-tech manufacturing, profits in computer, telecommunications, and other electronic equipment manufacturing doubled over the first ten months. Conversely, traditional sectors such as furniture manufacturing struggled immensely, posting a sharp profit decline of 52.4%. Upstream industries and artificial intelligence-related fields heavily outperformed downstream consumer markets, illustrating that the broader domestic economic recovery remains uneven and heavily reliant on specific export-driven pockets.

This two-speed recovery presents ongoing challenges for Chinese policymakers as weak domestic demand and persistent downturns in the property sector continue to weigh on corporate performance. Many domestic manufacturers have increasingly turned to overseas markets to sustain growth, exposing them to rising geopolitical tensions and potential Western trade restrictions. While Beijing has rolled out targeted monetary easing, liquidity injections, and interest-rate cuts, economists suggest that stronger household demand is essential for long-term stability. Furthermore, robust profit numbers have reduced expectations of near-term monetary policy easing by the central bank.

stories.title: Trump Demands Immediate Probe Into Revised Third-Quarter GDP Growth Figures
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump called for an urgent investigation into what he termed deliberate and massive errors regarding economic growth data issued prior to the midterm elections. On Wednesday, the US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis raised the third-quarter annualized growth rate to 4.3 percent, a notable increase from the initial estimate of 3.4 percent announced on October 29. Trump’s Republican Party subsequently experienced heavy defeats in the November 3 election. Speaking from his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, where he observed the Thanksgiving holiday, Trump asserted without evidence that the initial figures were fake and questioned why accurate data was withheld before voters went to the polls. He noted that a nearly full percentage point adjustment is unprecedented in history.

The Bureau of Economic Analysis did not respond to requests for comment on Thursday, though it has previously explained that early quarterly estimates lack complete source data covering inventories, trade, and consumer spending on services, which accounts for variances in final reports. Historical analysis indicates that substantial revisions are not entirely uncommon. A May article co-authored by BEA Director Vipin Arora and Rebecca Pocase revealed that the bureau has adjusted quarterly GDP estimates by nearly a full percentage point or more at least four times over the past 25 years. Furthermore, their research showed that calculations released 90 days after an initial estimate differed by an average of 0.52 percentage points throughout the current century. This controversy follows previous friction regarding federal data quality, notably when Trump terminated a top Labor Department official last year over unsubstantiated claims of figure manipulation.

stories.title: State Bank of Pakistan's Foreign Exchange Reserves Increase by $8 Million
stories.summary:
Foreign exchange reserves controlled by the State Bank of Pakistan experienced a modest increase during the week ending November 20. According to data released by the central bank on Thursday, reserves grew by $8 million, bringing the total held by the institution to $21.59 billion. This upward movement contributes to the broader financial standing of the nation.

When combined with holdings across commercial banks, the country's cumulative foreign reserves reached a total of $26.74 billion. Within this total, commercial financial institutions accounted for $5.15 billion. The central bank's weekly update provides a snapshot of the country's external account stability as financial authorities navigate ongoing economic adjustments and monetary benchmarks.

stories.title: Pakistani Minister Urges Seafood Exporters to Increase Value-Added Products
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s Maritime Affairs Minister, Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, has called upon seafood exporters to ensure that a minimum of five percent of their total sales consist of value-added products. This directive was issued during a meeting in Karachi on January 7 with members of the Korangi Association of Trade and Industry (KATI), aimed at identifying ways to boost seafood exports and enhance foreign exchange earnings. The minister highlighted that out of 578 seafood exporters in the country, only three currently handle processed seafood.

To address this gap and promote processed options, the minister established a dedicated committee led by Fisheries Development Commissioner Dr Muhammad Hafeez-ur-Rehman from the Ministry of Maritime Affairs. This panel will coordinate closely with provincial fisheries departments and industry exporters to explore growth opportunities and recommend expansion measures. The meeting included participation from provincial fisheries representatives via video link alongside senior officials from the ministries of maritime affairs and national food security.

Mr Chaudhry encouraged local businesses to initiate value-addition activities on a modest scale and progressively scale up their operations over time. He stressed the importance of investing in key operational areas such as processing and packaging to secure access to more lucrative international markets. The initiative forms part of broader government efforts to upgrade the fisheries sector and diversify exports beyond raw commodities.

Enhancing the share of processed seafood is vital for improving the country's trade competitiveness and maximizing economic returns from marine resources. By shifting focus toward value-added goods, Pakistani exporters can better navigate global market demands and increase sector profitability. The newly formed committee is expected to deliver actionable recommendations to facilitate this transition.

stories.title: New Zealand Coalition Falls Short, Needs Centrist Support to Govern
stories.summary:
New Zealand's ruling centre-right coalition has narrowly missed securing a parliamentary majority in the final election results released on Friday. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's government coalition finished with 65 seats in the 130-seat parliament, leaving them one seat short of an outright majority. Consequently, the administration must secure the backing of the centrist Opportunity Party to maintain power and establish a stable government for the full legislative term.

Prime Minister Luxon emphasized the necessity for a durable administration that can work collaboratively without rushing into unstable agreements or forcing new elections. In the November 7 election, Luxon’s National Party won 40 seats, while its junior partners, ACT and New Zealand First, secured 13 and 12 seats respectively. Meanwhile, the primary opposition party, Labour, captured 36 seats, and new parliamentary entrant Opportunity claimed seven seats.

Opportunity Party leader Qiulae Wong stated that her party is open to negotiations with all sides, emphasizing that stability remains a primary goal. However, Opportunity's policy platform includes stronger climate commitments, a ban on bottom-trawling, tighter competition rules, and greater public investment, which diverge from certain aspects of the ruling coalition's agenda. ACT Party leader David Seymour expressed optimism that a government could be formed rapidly if the parties cooperate effectively.

If the ruling coalition fails to reach an agreement with Opportunity, New Zealand could face fresh elections unless alternative coalition arrangements emerge. Although a centre-left bloc involving Labour, the Green Party, and Te Pati Maori cannot secure a majority even with Opportunity, potential realignments involving New Zealand First remain theoretically possible. Following the election results announcement, the New Zealand dollar saw a slight recovery after hitting a 17-year low against the US dollar earlier in the week.

stories.title: Australia Imposes Sanctions on Two Individuals Over Iran-Linked Arson Attacks
stories.summary:
Australia has enacted counterterrorism financing sanctions against two individuals accused of orchestrating antisemitic arson attacks in Sydney and Melbourne on behalf of Iran. Foreign Minister Penny Wong announced the measures on Friday, identifying the targeted individuals as Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad. According to Australian authorities, the pair utilized a complicated network of proxies to carry out attacks against a kosher restaurant in Sydney and the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne during 2024.

Foreign Minister Wong stated that the newly imposed sanctions are designed to restrict the suspects' access to financial resources and hinder their capacity to recruit operatives, plan operations, and execute future attacks. These actions represent a continuation of Canberra's firm response to hostile foreign interference and violent incidents targeting domestic communities and interests. The measures specifically aim to curtail the operational reach of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) within Australian jurisdiction.

Tensions between Australia and Iran escalated significantly prior to these sanctions. In August 2025, the Australian government ordered the expulsion of Iran’s ambassador—marking the first such diplomatic expulsion since World War Two—while also suspending operations at its embassy in Tehran and formally designating the IRGC as a terrorist organization. The latest financial restrictions underscore Canberra's ongoing strategy to dismantle networks associated with state-sponsored foreign aggression and protect national security.

stories.title: UN Warns Global Maritime Trade Faces Zero Growth in 2026
stories.summary:
Global maritime trade, which accounts for the transportation of over 80 percent of the world's goods, is projected to experience zero growth in 2026. According to a report released on Thursday by the United Nations trade and development agency UNCTAD, this stagnation follows a modest 1.9 percent expansion in 2025 and is driven by ongoing shipping disruptions and widespread trade uncertainty originating from the conflict in the Middle East.

The slowdown is heavily attributed to continuous disturbances in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping lane handling approximately one-fifth of global oil supplies alongside vital commodities like fertilizer. Before the crisis, roughly 120 vessels traversed the strait daily, but traffic measured by gross tonnage plummeted by about 95 percent by early March. Additionally, conflict spilling into the Red Sea and instability affecting Black Sea grain shipments and the Panama Canal have severely complicated logistics and triggered late-February oil price volatility.

These chokepoint closures have forced maritime carriers to divert vessels along longer routes around the Cape of Good Hope, significantly lengthening voyages and inflating operational costs and freight rate volatility. UNCTAD noted that while the utilization of alternative ports, inland transport networks, and new logistics solutions has managed to keep trade moving, it has come at a substantially higher financial price. These pressures pose particular risks to supply chains in developing nations.

stories.title: Gold prices rebound from one-year lows as holiday calm eases market jitters
stories.summary:
Gold prices experienced an upward movement on Friday, recovering from a greater than one-year low reached earlier in the week. This recovery was aided by a holiday lull in the United States, which helped reduce selling pressure and calmed market anxieties driven by artificial intelligence concerns. Spot gold advanced 1.6 percent to reach $3,622.91 per ounce by 0247 GMT, recovering from its weakest level since September 2025. This drop had originally occurred on Wednesday following strong domestic inflation readings that reinforced expectations of forthcoming interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. Additionally, US gold futures scheduled for December delivery rose by 2.6 percent to settle at $3,621.10. Ross Maxwell, chief strategy officer at VT Markets, noted that while bullion attempted to stabilize following recent losses, investors remain watchful. Market participants are paying close attention to real interest rates, the trajectory of the US dollar, and incoming investment flows to gauge the timing of any sustained recovery.

The broader financial environment reflected several competing pressures as the US economy expanded faster than initially anticipated during the third quarter. Inflation figures accelerated through October, supporting projections that the US central bank will raise borrowing costs at its next meeting and again early in 2027. These prospects increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, especially after the Federal Reserve implemented its first rate increase in three years back in September. Meanwhile, international trade figures showed that China's net gold imports via Hong Kong grew by 1.6 percent in October compared to the prior month, marking the highest volume recorded since April according to the Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department.

Other precious metals also tracked upward trajectories alongside gold during the weekly trading cycle. Spot silver recorded a 4.6 percent increase to reach $43.40 per ounce, platinum advanced by 2.6 percent to trade at $1,323.78, and palladium moved higher by 3.3 percent to close at $901.50. All three of these metals were positioned to close the week with positive gains. Asian equities similarly prepared to finish out a difficult month with greater stability as the holiday period offered temporary relief from broader technology sector selloffs and asset liquidations on Wall Street, which had remained closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

stories.title: Automakers in Pakistan accelerate electric bike rollouts amidst fluctuating fuel prices
stories.summary:
Industry stakeholders in Pakistan are advancing plans to test and introduce new electric motorcycles in the local market, capitalising on fluctuating fuel costs. Current electric bike prices vary between Rs170,000 and Rs700,000 across different model variants. At the same time, major traditional manufacturers continue to register strong sales for petrol-powered vehicles. Atlas Honda reported record sales of 173,152 units during the preceding month, bringing its aggregate total for the first four months of fiscal year 2027 to 643,561 units, up from 505,269 units in the corresponding period previously. United Motorcycle also saw an increase, with sales climbing to 82,474 units from 56,519 units.

New entrants are entering the segment with significant production targets. Millat Tractors Ltd is scheduled to launch its lithium-ion-powered two-wheelers on November 29, having already designated dealers and initiated production. Its subsidiary, Millat Industrial, will manufacture five variants of bikes and scooters with an annual production capacity of 250,000 units. Similarly, Air Link Communication Limited launched its AirV electric bikes on November 4 from the Sundar Green Special Economic Zone, targeting an annual capacity of 100,000 units. According to data from Topline Securities, Air Link plans to price its vehicles between Rs200,000 and Rs500,000 without offering credit sales, while initially importing 10,000 to 15,000 units before scaling local output based on market reception.

Government initiatives are supporting the transition through financial incentives, including a Rs50,000 subsidy from the Punjab government and an 80,000-rupee subsidy offered through the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification programme. Over the past year, electric bike sales surpassed 300,000 units, with Punjab recording the highest adoption rates while Karachi showed moderate growth. However, an analysis by the Institute of Cost and Management Accountants of Pakistan warns that the transition risks replacing dependency on imported petroleum with reliance on imported electric technology unless policy focuses on building a domestic manufacturing base. The report also highlights a gap in financing, noting that banks processed only 9,889 of 44,689 loan applications by May 31, granting approval to just 4,075 cases.

stories.title: PTI distances itself from Achakzai's premature proposal for a national government
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf has distanced itself from Mahmood Khan Achakzai's recent call for a national government and extensive political and constitutional reforms. Although the party refrained from issuing an official public statement, senior figures clarified their stance through background discussions with media representatives. This development indicates that the alliance chief failed to consult partner parties prior to making his proposal public. A similar lack of coordination occurred a few months prior when the PTI unilaterally announced a protest march toward Islamabad, exposing underlying fractures within the opposition alliance.

During a conference held in Lahore, Mr Achakzai emphasized parliamentary sovereignty, constitutional supremacy, and democratic restoration, alongside raising valid concerns regarding deteriorating security conditions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, and Azad Jammu and Kashmir. Despite these pressing issues, analysts suggest that demanding a national government is premature and offers no concrete solution to ongoing political uncertainty. Introducing an undefined political arrangement risks deepening existing divisions rather than resolving them. Furthermore, the public contradictions among alliance leaders damage their credibility, raising questions about whether representatives speak for the entire coalition or solely for their individual factions.

To build public trust and present a viable alternative, opposition parties are advised to utilize the remainder of the parliamentary term by pressing the administration on critical governance matters. Key areas requiring legislative focus include protecting civil liberties, halting restrictions on freedom of expression, addressing political prisoners, and restoring normal administrative functions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Additionally, both political sides must begin preparing necessary arrangements for free, fair, and credible upcoming elections, which involves securing institutional neutrality and establishing a safe environment for all competing entities. Engaging constructively within parliament remains the most effective path for the opposition to demonstrate a genuine commitment to parliamentary democracy.

stories.title: IAEA mediates local ceasefire to repair power lines at Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
stories.summary:
The United Nations nuclear watchdog announced on Thursday that it is actively collaborating with Russian and Ukrainian authorities to facilitate a local ceasefire. This diplomatic effort aims to allow repair teams to restore external power lines at the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant. Russian military forces captured the facility, which stands as Europe's largest nuclear plant featuring six reactors, during the initial weeks of the February 2022 invasion. Since then, both conflicting parties have frequently accused one another of conducting military operations that threaten overall nuclear safety in the active war zone.

Although the facility is currently not generating electricity, it requires a steady external power supply to ensure that the nuclear fuel inside its reactors remains properly cooled. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, both main external power lines have now failed for the 28th time since the conflict began, forcing the plant to rely on emergency diesel generators. The agency attributed the latest outage to military activity in the vicinity. Meanwhile, Russian operators at the site reported that the disconnection happened automatically after protection devices activated, adding that the backup diesel generators were functioning normally.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi described the situation as extremely precarious due to the facility's direct positioning along the front line of an active combat zone. He urged both warring nations to cooperate constructively with the watchdog by pausing military actions near the site to enable urgent repair work. The Zaporizhzhia plant has repeatedly faced vulnerabilities regarding its offsite power connections throughout the prolonged conflict, prompting continuous international monitoring and diplomatic interventions by the IAEA to prevent potential nuclear accidents.

stories.title: اسلام آباد میں مکہ دفاعی اتحاد کے اجلاس میں سعودی سکیورٹی پر غور
stories.summary:
جمعے کو اسلام آباد میں مکہ دفاعی اتحاد کے رکن ممالک پاکستان، ترکی اور سعودی عرب کی اسٹریٹجک پولیٹیکل اینڈ ڈیفنس کمیٹی کا اجلاس منعقد ہو رہا ہے۔ وزیر دفاع خواجہ آصف نے اے ایف پی سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے تصدیق کی ہے کہ اجلاس کے ایجنڈے میں سعودی عرب کے جنوب میں موجودہ کشیدگی اور ریاض و یمن کے حوثیوں کے درمیان تنازع کو اہم حیثیت حاصل ہوگی۔ اس اجلاس میں تینوں ممالک کے وزرائے خارجہ اور وزرائے دفاع شریک ہیں، اور اس کے انعقاد کے پیش نظر اسلام آباد کی مقامی انتظامیہ نے شہر میں عام تعطیل کا اعلان کیا ہے۔

رواں سال اگست میں طے پانے والے اس مشترکہ دفاعی معاہدے کے تحت ایک رکن ملک پر حملہ تمام رکن ممالک پر حملہ تصور کیا جاتا ہے۔ اس سے قبل اکتوبر کے مہینے میں اس کمیٹی کا پہلا ہنگامی اجلاس ریاض میں ہوا تھا جس میں اجتماعی دفاعی ذمہ داریوں اور عسکری صلاحیتوں کے نفاذ کا فیصلہ کیا گیا تھا۔ پاکستان کے وزیر دفاع خواجہ آصف کا کہنا ہے کہ سعودی عرب کے خلاف کوئی بھی خطرہ پاکستان کے خلاف خطرہ سمجھا جائے گا، جبکہ انہوں نے خطے میں اسرائیل کو بھی ایک خطرہ قرار دیا۔

اس معاہدے کے تحت پاکستان اور ترکی پہلے ہی اپنی پوزیشن واضح کر چکے ہیں۔ پاکستانی فوج کے ترجمان نے انٹرویو میں تصدیق کی ہے کہ مختلف صلاحیتوں کے حامل پاکستانی دستے سعودی عرب میں موجود ہیں، جو دہائیوں پرانی دفاعی تعاون کا تسلسل ہے۔ اسی طرح ترک پارلیمان نے بھی اس سولہ شقوں پر مشتمل معاہدے کی باضابطہ توثیق کر دی ہے، جس کی شقوں کے مطابق تمام فریقین بیرونی مسلح حملے کی صورت میں اقوام متحدہ کے منشور کی شق 51 کے تحت باہمی امداد فراہم کرنے کے پابند ہوں گے۔

ترک پارلیمان کی خارجہ امور کمیٹی کے سربراہ فؤاد اوکتائے نے واضح کیا تھا کہ یہ اتحاد مکمل طور پر دفاعی نوعیت کا ہے اور اس کا مقصد کسی دوسرے ملک پر جارحیت کرنا نہیں ہے۔ معاہدے کی دیگر شقوں میں دہشت گردی کے خلاف مشترکہ کوششیں، دفاعی صنعت میں ٹیکنالوجی کا تبادلہ، مشترکہ تربیتی پروگرام اور انٹیلی جنس و سکیورٹی کے شعبوں میں تعاون کو فروغ دینا شامل ہے تاکہ خطے کے استحکام کو یقینی بنایا جا سکے۔

stories.title: Trump Says Vladimir Putin Is Welcome to Attend Florida G20 Summit
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump stated on Thursday that Russian President Vladimir Putin would be permitted to attend the upcoming G20 summit in Florida if he wished to participate. Speaking to reporters from his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, while spending the Thanksgiving holiday, Trump expressed his personal desire to have Putin at the meeting, acknowledging simultaneously that some individuals would oppose his presence and expressing doubt that Putin would actually want to come. The high-profile gathering is scheduled for December 14-15.

Responding to the remarks, the Kremlin announced on Thursday that no official determination has been reached regarding Putin's travel plans for the summit. Putin himself mentioned following a meeting with Trump the previous week that he would evaluate attending after conferring with the US president, though he emphasized the need to factor in domestic conditions within Russia before deciding on a trip to the United States. Earlier on Thursday, Trump used a Truth Social post to call for Russia to scale back its military aggression across European territories to potentially foster a swift resolution to the ongoing war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Islamabad Hosts Makkah Defence Alliance Meeting to Address Regional Security
stories.summary:
Pakistan is hosting a two-day meeting of the tripartite Makkah Defence Alliance's top decision-making body, the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC), in Islamabad. Authorities have declared a public holiday in the capital along with special movement restrictions, and a local holiday has also been announced in nearby Rawalpindi. The gathering brings together the foreign ministers, defence ministers, and chiefs of defence staff from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye to focus on establishing institutional frameworks, coordination mechanisms, and standard operating procedures.

Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif noted that persistent turmoil south of Saudi Arabia remains a primary agenda point, driven by repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi cities, oil infrastructure, and shipping lanes. The alliance, established under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed on August 7, stipulates that an armed aggression against any single member constitutes an assault on all three, requiring mutual assistance including military support. While Turkiye completed its accession through ratification and a permanent secretariat was established in Riyadh under retired Pakistani Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood as secretary general, the coalition's operational framework remains in its early stages as members navigate wider regional tensions involving Iran, the United States, and Israel.

stories.title: Mercedes-Benz Establishes New Joint Venture in Beijing for Local Parts Sourcing
stories.summary:
German automaker Mercedes-Benz is moving forward with plans to create a new joint venture in Beijing dedicated to procuring passenger vehicle components. According to a regulatory filing submitted to China's market regulator on Friday, the newly formed entity will supply locally sourced parts directly to the company's existing manufacturing partnership with BAIC Motor.

Under the proposed ownership structure detailed in the filing, Mercedes-Benz China will maintain a dominant 70 percent stake in the newly established procurement company. Meanwhile, Beijing Benz, the primary manufacturing joint venture between the German automotive giant and BAIC, will retain the remaining 30 percent interest. Both corporate entities will share joint control over the operations of the new venture.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Sustains Rally Despite Rising Oil Prices and Dollar Strength
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is maintaining its position as Asia's top-performing currency this month, gaining 2.6% despite facing fresh pressure from climbing oil prices. Brent crude recently surpassed the $96 threshold due to heightened supply disruption worries and an escalating Middle East risk premium. The currency was anticipated to open relatively flat after settling at 92.4450 against the US dollar on Thursday.

Strong foreign equity inflows are providing a substantial cushion for the rupee, as international investors increasingly rotate out of artificial intelligence-related assets amid sustainability concerns. Preliminary data showed foreign investors purchasing over $600 million in Indian shares on Thursday, pushing November inflows to $16 billion and erasing roughly half of the outflows recorded during the first ten months of the year. This shift in market sentiment is further evidenced by options trading, where positioning for a rupee rally currently commands a higher cost than betting on a decline, contrasting with the broader US dollar index hovering near a 22-month high.

stories.title: Global Markets Balance as Dollar Strengthens and Asian Stocks Steady
stories.summary:
Global financial markets experienced varied outcomes as Asian shares worked toward ending a difficult month on a stable trajectory, aided by a holiday slowdown that temporarily eased artificial intelligence anxieties. Meanwhile, the US dollar advanced firmly on safe-haven demand and growing expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike, positioning itself for a third consecutive monthly gain.

In regional trading, S&P 500 futures rose 0.8% and Nasdaq futures increased 1% following the Thanksgiving holiday closure on Wall Street. Japan's Nikkei advanced 0.7%, though it maintained an 8.4% loss for the month. Tokyo core inflation hit a 16-month high in November, reinforcing expectations for a Bank of Japan rate increase as early as next month. Elsewhere, MSCI's broader index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan gained 0.5%, while South Korean shares rallied 2% and Chinese blue chips dipped slightly to their lowest level since June 2025.

Technology sector concerns persisted, marked by S&P placing Nvidia's credit rating on watch for a potential downgrade and reports that the chipmaker instructed manufacturing partners to halt server shipments containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. In other corporate news, Elon Musk pledged about $18 billion worth of shares in his space and AI company SpaceX, promising two shares to every child in the United States.

The US dollar index stood at 103.8, supported by futures indicating a 99% probability that the Federal Reserve will raise rates by 25 basis points in December. European markets noted the expected succession of Pablo Hernández de Cos as the upcoming European Central Bank president, signaling policy continuity. Meanwhile, New Zealand's dollar edged up after the ruling centre-right coalition fell short of a parliamentary majority, requiring negotiations with the Opportunity Party to govern.

stories.title: US Dollar Hovers Near Peak Amid Fed Rate Hike Expectations
stories.summary:
The US currency remained close to a 22-month high during a holiday-thinned trading session, with market participants closely monitoring equity performance and artificial intelligence sector volatility to gauge future currency directions. Analysts note that currency fluctuations heavily depend on whether the recent downturn in AI-related equities reverses or prompts further defensive safe-haven flows.

The dollar index, which tracks the currency against six major counterparts, held steady at 103.81. Earlier in the week, the index touched 104.53—its highest level since March of the previous year—before erasing those gains. During early Asian trading, the dollar edged up 0.1% to 159.355 yen and ticked higher against the Swiss franc at 0.83455. Meanwhile, the euro remained virtually unchanged at $1.0964, sterling eased slightly to $1.3099, and the risk-sensitive Australian dollar softened to $0.6631 following a one-year low earlier in the week.

Support for the American currency continues to be driven by anticipated Federal Reserve monetary tightening. According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, traders view a quarter-point interest rate increase on December 9 as nearly certain. Additional confidence stems from stronger-than-expected October core personal consumption expenditures inflation, an upward revision to third-quarter gross domestic product, and a Federal Reserve survey indicating persistent economic expansion and sticky inflation, raising expectations for another potential hike around April.

With the dollar index climbing approximately 5.7% throughout the year with only a month remaining, strategists at National Australia Bank suggest the currency is tracking a stronger-for-longer trajectory than previously anticipated. However, they caution that given its rapid upward movement, the scope for further short-term gains remains limited.

stories.title: AJK Government Launches Rs15 Billion Reform Package for 100 Days
stories.summary:
The PML-N-led Azad Jammu and Kashmir government announced a Rs15 billion, 100-day action plan designed to enhance healthcare, education, transport, tourism, and civic infrastructure. Cabinet members detailed both immediate initiatives and long-term projects during a press briefing aimed at accelerating regional development and delivering essential public amenities.

Under the healthcare sector, Health and Population Welfare Minister Dr Mustafa Bashir Abbasi announced the Sehat Karwan initiative, deploying 70 mobile hospital units to remote areas alongside an Essential Medicines Programme to secure life-saving drugs and dialysis capabilities. Plans also include establishing 20 model basic health units, 10 model rural health centres, and upgrading district and divisional hospitals. Education Minister Sardar Umair Naeem introduced the Darsgah project for out-of-school children, a cellular biometric attendance system to combat absenteeism, the construction of five Daanish Schools, a Daanish University in Muzaffarabad, and the distribution of 5,000 merit-based laptops.

To improve transport and civic services, Forests and Wildlife Minister Waqar Ahmad Noor announced the Kashmir Express Service featuring 75 electric buses across seven cities, alongside urban beautification projects and the Suthra Kashmir campaign. Tourism Minister Chaudhry Abdul Rehman Arain highlighted eco-tourism and adventure initiatives, alongside housing loans and public-private partnerships for guest houses. Separately, Prime Minister Iftikhar Gillani informed the AJK Legislative Assembly that his administration is working to resolve challenges and complete the 93% finished 48-megawatt Jagran-II hydropower project in Neelum Valley, which faced delays following the pandemic, civil unrest, and the withdrawal of its Chinese contractor.

stories.title: Brent Crude Stays Near Monthly High Amid Middle East Supply Fears
stories.summary:
Oil prices hovered near monthly highs as persistent security incidents involving tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure, and Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries raised global supply concerns. Both major crude benchmarks are heading toward their first weekly increase in four weeks.

Brent crude futures declined slightly by 38 cents, or 0.39%, to $96.19 a barrel following a nearly $2 gain that marked its highest settlement since November 6. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures traded at $85.41 a barrel, reflecting a 2.07% increase from Wednesday's close, with no settlement recorded on Thursday due to the US Thanksgiving holiday. Analysts from ANZ noted that Brent could potentially surpass $100 per barrel even without a major regional escalation if deliverable supply constraints become more apparent.

Supply disruptions have intensified following continued attacks on shipping lanes by Iran and targeted strikes by Yemeni Houthis on Saudi energy assets. Saudi Arabia’s Energy Ministry reported that a projectile struck Saudi Aramco’s Jazan refinery, resulting in one death and multiple injuries, following previous Houthi claims targeting Ras Tanura and Red Sea ports. Amid these geopolitical tensions, OPEC+ sources indicated the group is likely to maintain its oil output targets for the first quarter of 2027 during an upcoming Sunday meeting.

Simultaneously, international refining capacity faced additional pressures from Ukrainian drone strikes causing a fire at Russia’s Slavyansk ECO refinery, alongside separate industrial incidents at Thailand’s Bangchak refinery, Venezuela’s Amuay refinery, and an offshore disruption at Brazil’s Bacalhau oilfield operated by Equinor and Galp.

stories.title: Pakistan Auto Sector Faces Decades of Stagnation Amid Economic Pressures
stories.summary:
Automobile sales in Pakistan have stagnated over the past twenty years due to persistent economic instability, weak consumer purchasing power, and fluctuating government policies. Industry leaders point out that despite a collective annual manufacturing capacity of 600,000 units, local car sales stood at 148,000 units in 2025 compared to 152,000 units in 2005. This lack of growth is viewed not as a supply failure, but as a direct result of recurring macroeconomic disruptions and limited access to affordable auto financing.

Representatives from the Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts & Accessories Manufacturers (PAAPAM) and the Pakistan Automotive Manufacturers Association (PAMA) highlighted these challenges. PAAPAM Chairman Abdul Rehman Aizaz and PAMA Director General Razi-ur-Rahman noted that previous policy targets, such as those under the Auto Industry Development Programme, fell short of expectations. Currently, approximately 16 players compete for the market, which diminishes individual production volumes and weakens investments in component localization. Gallup data indicates that only about six to seven percent of Pakistani households own a passenger vehicle, translating to roughly 11 car owners per 1,000 people.

Discussions regarding the upcoming Auto Policy 2026-31 have faced delays due to lack of recent stakeholder engagement and complications involving Pakistan's ongoing International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme. Certain proposed provisions, such as mandatory export requirements and minimum local value addition, have raised concerns from the fund regarding potential unfair trade practices. Industry experts emphasize that any future framework requires careful evaluation and primary focus on job creation to support the nation's population of 255 million.

Addressing these policy hurdles is crucial for balancing the interests of local component vendors, international automakers, and the transition toward electric vehicles. Stakeholders warn that failure to properly manage the sector risks encouraging excessive imports of parts and completely built-up vehicles, which would further strain foreign exchange reserves. A comprehensive strategy through wider consultations remains necessary to foster sustainable growth in the country's automotive manufacturing landscape.

stories.title: Sindh Chief Minister Announces Consultations on New Local Government Law
stories.summary:
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah announced a broad consultation process in Karachi on November 26 regarding a new local government framework. Speaking at a press conference at the CM House alongside provincial ministers and Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, Shah formed a two-member ministerial committee consisting of Syed Nasir Hussain Shah and Ziaul Hassan Lanjar to engage with political parties, civil society, and other stakeholders, with a mandate to submit a report within three months.

The initiative comes amid public discussions concerning the establishment of new administrative units and provinces across Pakistan, including Sindh, a concept strongly opposed by the Pakistan Peoples Party. The chief minister stressed that the upcoming legislation will arrive through amendments to the current local government law, and confirmed that the next local government polls will occur on schedule despite challenging political and security conditions.

The proposed legal changes aim to grant greater financial and administrative autonomy to local bodies, with funding enhancements to be determined via the Provincial Finance Commission. Responding to queries regarding a potential referendum on new provinces, Shah noted that nobody had approached him regarding such a process and recalled that the Sindh Assembly previously rejected boundary divisions within the province by a two-thirds majority.

The ongoing political discourse matters because it touches directly on administrative decentralization and provincial integrity in Pakistan. Strengthening local governments and addressing grassroots governance remains a critical priority for local leaders, making the committee's upcoming stakeholder recommendations pivotal for regional policy.

stories.title: کراچی میں غیر قانونی عمارت گرنے سے اموات 6 ہو گئیں
stories.summary:
کراچی کی ایڈمنسٹریشن سوسائٹی میں ایک غیر قانونی طور پر تعمیر کی جانے والی رہائشی عمارت اچانک زمین بوس ہو گئی، جس کے نتیجے میں جاں بحق ہونے والے افراد کی تعداد بڑھ کر 6 ہو گئی ہے۔ اس افسوسناک حادثے میں کل 13 افراد تاحال لاپتا ہیں۔ حکام کے مطابق اس حادثے میں جان کی بازی ہارنے والے افراد میں 6 بچے، 2 خواتین اور 3 مرد شامل ہیں۔

ابتدائی تحقیقات اور اطلاعات کے مطابق یہ حادثہ بدھ کے روز پیش آیا جہاں 600 گز کے رہائشی پلاٹ پر چھ منزلہ عمارت بنا دی گئی تھی۔ اس عمارت کا منظور شدہ نقشہ صرف گراؤنڈ پلس ون کا تھا، لیکن اس پر قواعد کے خلاف پانچ اضافی منزلیں تعمیر کر لی گئی تھیں اور چھٹی منزل پر کام ابھی جاری تھا۔

واقعے کے بعد صوبائی حکومت اور انتظامیہ حرکت میں آ گئی ہے۔ وزیر اعلیٰ سندھ نے بتایا کہ شہر میں اس وقت 143 عمارتیں حکمِ امتناع پر زیرِ تعمیر ہیں اور ان تمام عمارتوں پر فوری طور پر کام رکوا دیا گیا ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ انتظامیہ نے شہر بھر میں بغیر اجازت کے زیرِ تعمیر ایسی تمام 143 عمارتوں کو سیل کرنے کے احکامات بھی جاری کر دیے ہیں۔

حکومتی احکامات میں واضح کیا گیا ہے کہ عدالتوں کی طرف سے حکم امتناع حاصل ہونے کی صورت میں بھی تمام غیر قانونی تعمیرات کو فوری طور پر روکا جائے گا۔ اس واقعے نے شہر میں عمارتوں کی غیر قانونی تعمیرات اور حفاظتی قوانین کی خلاف ورزیوں پر ایک بار پھر سنگین سوالات کھڑے کر دیے ہیں، جن پر قابو پانے کے لیے انتظامیہ سخت اقدامات کر رہی ہے۔

stories.title: Punjab Revenue Authority Cracks Down on Businesses Evading Electronic Invoices
stories.summary:
The Punjab Revenue Authority (PRA) has intensified its enforcement operations across multiple divisions in Pakistan, targeting commercial entities failing to install or correctly utilize the Electronic Invoice Monitoring System (e-IMS). Special monitoring teams are active across the Lahore, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Rawalpindi, and Multan divisions to ensure compliance with digital sales reporting mandates.

During these recent field inspections, enforcement officers issued show-cause notices to more than 65 business operators found violating e-IMS guidelines. A PRA spokesperson emphasized that the agency will pursue legal action against establishments engaging in sales record manipulation, issuing fake receipts, or attempting to bypass tax obligations. Operators have been formally instructed to issue computerized receipts and maintain transparent tax logs, with severe penalties awaiting non-compliant businesses.

The digital monitoring rollout seeks to curb widespread tax evasion and enhance accountability within provincial revenue collection. Additionally, the authority encourages consumer participation by utilizing QR codes printed on computerized receipts, which enable customers to independently verify charged taxes in real time.

This enforcement drive matters because systematic tax compliance is vital for strengthening public finances and improving economic transparency in the region. By enforcing digital tracking, the PRA aims to close loopholes that have historically undermined revenue mobilization.

stories.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif Establishes Committee to Implement Jamaat-e-Islami Relief Proposals
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced the creation of a specialized oversight committee in Islamabad on Thursday to review and implement economic relief proposals put forward by a Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) delegation led by party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman. Meeting at a time of severe public pressure over soaring petroleum prices and living costs, the prime minister assured the delegation that the administration would execute viable recommendations in good faith.

Reflecting on past relief efforts following the Iran-US conflict, the prime minister noted that the federal government deployed Rs128 billion for nationwide subsidies before expanding targeted relief to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws, and vehicles up to 800cc. According to government figures, these emergency measures directly aided roughly 20 million citizens and indirectly benefited nearly 100 million people.

Following discussions, JI chief Rehman told reporters that the administration agreed to expand fuel relief to vehicles up to 1,000cc and deliver agricultural assistance for farmers owning up to 12.5 acres, including tractor-related support. Furthermore, authorities agreed to reduce the petroleum levy impact from Rs80 to Rs63 ahead of the next budget, phase out official vehicles exceeding 1,600cc, and review existing agreements with independent power producers. Rehman noted that lower power tariffs and IPP revisions have already reduced electricity bills by 25 percent over the past two years.

This agreement matters because it represents a major policy dialogue between the ruling administration and opposition figures aimed at easing financial distress for millions of Pakistanis. The newly formed committee will monitor ongoing progress, while JI maintains its broader political pressure pending a major rally in Lahore.

stories.title: Industry Leaders Urge Technology Upgrades for Pakistan's Stone and Mineral Sector
stories.summary:
Sanaullah Khan, former Chairman of the All Pakistan Marble Industries Association (APMIA), underscored Pakistan's immense potential to develop into a prominent global hub for dimension stone trade, production, and processing during a high-level meeting in Karachi. The discussions brought together Italian diplomatic and trade officials, including Italian Consul General Fabrizio Bielli, Italian Trade Agency Director Dr. Salvatore Parano, and technical experts Engr. Paolo Marone and Engr. Claudia Chiappino.

The meeting convened prominent Pakistani quarry owners, mining representatives, and entrepreneurs dealing in marble, granite, onyx, and other natural minerals. Khan highlighted the critical need to modernize the domestic mining industry, improve processing efficiency, minimize material wastage, and boost the international standing of Pakistani stone products. The collaborative framework is coordinated alongside Confindustria Marmomacchine and the Italian Trade Agency.

Participants focused on introducing advanced Italian quarrying machinery, modern processing technology, and strict international quality standards to transform Pakistan's mineral sector from a raw-material exporter into a high-value, technology-driven industry. The visiting Italian delegation welcomed the proposals and expressed strong interest in fostering bilateral commercial ties, knowledge exchange, and technical cooperation.

This industrial engagement matters because upgrading Pakistan's mineral sector can unlock substantial export revenue and drive sustainable economic growth. By combining Italian engineering expertise with abundant local natural resources, the partnership aims to elevate the country's manufacturing capacity on the world stage.

stories.title: PACCC Chief Urges Pakistani Businesses to Enhance Global Market Competitiveness
stories.summary:
Naveed Anwar Chaudhry, President of the Pak American Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce (PACCC), has called upon Pakistani enterprises to elevate product and service quality to satisfy international criteria. Speaking at a reception hosted in his honor at the National Press Club on Thursday, Chaudhry emphasized that strengthening global market competitiveness is essential for expanding exports, drawing foreign investment, and improving Pakistan's overall economic standing, with a particular focus on gaining access to the United States market.

Chaudhry pointed out that the Pakistan Business Forum Europe (PBFE) actively promotes trade collaboration among the Pakistani diaspora in the US and Europe, offering crucial guidance to local businesses entering foreign markets. He also noted that trade volumes between Pakistan and the Chicagoland Midwest region have grown since the Chamber's inception, demonstrating a clear appetite for heightened economic cooperation. Furthermore, he underscored the significance of youth entrepreneurship, mentioning that the Chamber provides dedicated mentorship and business training to help young Pakistanis meaningfully contribute to national development.

Highlighting avenues for collaboration, Chaudhry shared that American business sectors have expressed keen interest in investing in Pakistan. He encouraged local entrepreneurs and exporters to aggressively engage in trade roadshows and international exhibitions across the United States to display their goods, build networks with international buyers, and enhance the reputation of "Made in Pakistan" as a trusted global brand.

The initiative aims to bolster the country's export-led growth by fostering robust business-to-business partnerships and helping local industries secure necessary international certifications. Chaudhry reiterated his dedication to establishing a solid international identity for Pakistani products, asserting that coordinated efforts and strategic trade relationships are vital for long-term economic progress.

stories.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Government Formally Launches Guardianship Standard Operating Procedures
stories.summary:
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government officially launched Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for guardianship during the provincial World Children’s Day 2026 event held at the Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum Auditorium in Peshawar on Thursday. Dr. Aamer Abdullah, Advisor to the Governor for Education and Social Welfare, served as the chief guest for the occasion, which was organized by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Child Protection and Welfare Commission. Key officials, UNICEF representatives, civil society members, and children attended the gathering.

During the ceremony, the Commission signed Terms of Reference for mutual cooperation with renowned social worker and religious scholar Waliullah Maroof, officially designating him as the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Child Protection Brand Ambassador. Maroof will voluntarily assist in tracing missing children and reuniting them with their families. Dr. Abdullah praised Maroof's extensive humanitarian record, noting his successful efforts over the past five to six years in resolving complex family separation cases, some spanning nearly three decades.

According to data presented at the event, the Commission has reached 35,764 children, offered legal aid to 7,890 children and families, and successfully resolved 3,456 missing children cases. Additionally, the network is expanding with the addition of five new units to the existing 12 Child Protection Units across districts. The newly introduced SOPs, developed alongside UNICEF, aim to streamline the guardianship framework and are supported by an online digital database and portal to improve transparency and tracking.

Dr. Abdullah emphasized that ensuring child welfare requires unified participation from families, communities, and institutions. He also welcomed Helvetas Pakistan's plan to deliver technical and vocational skills training to 800 children, underscoring the government's commitment to broadening institutional partnerships and strengthening district-level child protection systems to prevent exploitation and neglect.

stories.title: Pakistan Customs Seizes Boat Carrying 40,000 Liters of Smuggled Diesel
stories.summary:
Pakistan Customs’ Marine Enforcement Unit in Gwadar successfully intercepted and seized a vessel carrying 40,000 liters of smuggled high-speed diesel off the Balochistan coast. Authorities valued the confiscated fuel and the boat, named Al-Behar-e-Amber, at approximately Rs40 million.

Officials reported that the operation was launched following specific intelligence regarding illegal fuel smuggling operations conducted via maritime routes. The enforcement team tracked and pursued the suspect vessel through harsh sea conditions for over 72 hours before successfully boarding and securing it.

Following the interception, legal actions were initiated against the individuals involved in accordance with applicable laws. While the department did not specify the precise origin of the fuel or the exact number of arrests made, they confirmed that the action forms part of a broader, ongoing anti-smuggling campaign led by Marine Enforcement Units in Gwadar and Gadani to eradicate the illegal petroleum trade along the coast.

stories.title: Islamabad Court Reserves Verdict on Appeal Challenging Judicial Magistrate's Order
stories.summary:
The District and Sessions Court in Islamabad on Thursday reserved its judgment on an appeal that challenges a judicial magistrate's ruling in a high-profile case. The case involves the mysterious death of 13-year-old domestic worker Fatima Asghar, who allegedly suffered physical torture while residing at the home of Afshan—the wife of an FIA Director—and Qari Ali Raza.

Additional District and Session Judge Raja Asif heard extensive arguments from both defense and prosecution counsels before reserving the final verdict. Akmal Khan, the defense counsel, argued that Judicial Magistrate Naima Iffat had overstepped her legal boundaries and assumed the role of an investigating officer, pointing out alleged contradictions in the magistrate's order and claiming that defense evidence was omitted from the official record.

Conversely, Special Prosecutor Wajid Munir strongly urged the court to dismiss the defense appeal. He maintained that the area magistrate acted well within her supervisory authority and that the ongoing police investigation into the tragic death of the young girl is proceeding correctly under Section 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code and related statutes.

The underlying written order by the judicial magistrate had directed investigators to scrutinize various aspects of the case, including determining the exact age of the deceased, verifying the relationship between the victim's family and the accused, and investigating potential child labor violations or financial arrangements under the Islamabad Capital Territory Domestic Workers Act and the Pakistan Penal Code.

stories.title: CDA Pledges to Share Service Delivery Timelines with Islamabad Business Community
stories.summary:
The Capital Development Authority has committed to sharing clear service delivery timelines with the Islamabad business community to enhance transparency and efficiency. During a visit to the Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry, CDA Director of One Window Operations Chaudhry Abdul Rauf announced that the civic body is transitioning toward a fully cashless system by November 30. Additionally, a new digital portal is being created to support online applications, case tracking, and prompt objection notifications.

Rauf noted that roughly 24 to 25 public services are currently managed through the One Window facility under established timeframes. For instance, residential No Demand Certificates have a prescribed four-day turnaround, while straightforward property transfers without legal or administrative hurdles are processed within a single day. The authority has also implemented a cashless payment approach utilizing electronic challans to streamline and secure financial transactions.

ICCI President Mohammad Zikria Akbar Zia stressed the critical need for robust institutional cooperation between the Chamber and the CDA to resolve administrative bottlenecks and tackle public grievances. Other chamber leaders pointed out that commercial stakeholders still encounter delays regarding property transfers and NOCs, emphasizing the importance of advanced notice for expected completion periods and immediate SMS alerts for any application deficiencies.

The discussions underscored the shared goal of improving civic administration to support Islamabad’s growing population and expanding commercial activities. Both organizations agreed that closer liaison and further digitalization of services will foster a more responsive, accountable, and citizen-friendly environment for residents and business owners alike.

stories.title: Scientist Urges Greater Investment in Research and Technology at Bilateral Event
stories.summary:
Renowned scientist Professor Dr. Atta-ur-Rahman advocated for heightened financial backing in research, innovation, and technology during a recent seminar in Karachi. Held at the Chinese Consulate, the China–Pakistan Youth Dialogue was jointly organized by the Economic Diplomacy Forum and the Chinese Consulate to celebrate the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China.

Dr. Atta-ur-Rahman, who previously served as Federal Minister for Science and Technology and founding chairman of the Higher Education Commission, urged Pakistan to emulate China's development framework. He emphasized the necessity of expanding research grants, offering tax incentives for private research and development, and creating contemporary technology zones alongside advanced research laboratories. Key figures, including Acting Consul General Dr. Feng Deheng and EDF founder President Dr. Muhammad Farooq Afzal, also addressed the attendees regarding educational cooperation and the evolving scope of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.

The event featured participation from university vice chancellors, academic experts, and students from multiple institutions in Pakistan, alongside virtual contributions from students at China's Sichuan Normal University. Discussions focused on deepening bilateral ties through joint academic programs, scientific research, and youth engagement. Leaders from both nations highlighted that future collaboration must heavily involve universities, entrepreneurs, and young professionals to build a sustainable knowledge-based economy.

stories.title: Conflicting Claims Emerge Over JUI-F Chief Fazl's Reported Arrest in Lahore
stories.summary:
Conflicting statements surfaced in Lahore regarding the reported detention of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman near Thokar Niaz Baig. A local JUI-F official maintained that party leader Fazl had been taken into custody by Lahore Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Bilal Siddique Kamyana and DIG Operations Faisal Kamran. Conversely, the DIG Operations firmly denied the arrest, stating that Fazl had safely returned to his residence with his convoy and that traffic on Multan Road and the motorway remained completely unhindered.

The contradictory claims arrived amid growing friction over JUI-F demonstrations and restrictions placed on the party's scheduled political activities across Punjab. Prior to the incident, the party approached the Lahore High Court after alleging that authorities had confined Fazl to his home and cordoned off his residence. The petition requested his immediate recovery and an urgent hearing so he could attend an all-parties conference arranged by the Lahore High Court Bar Association. Police maintained they neither arrested nor formally placed him under house arrest.

Political friction between Fazl and the federal administration has escalated since mid-October, driven by his opposition to the Centre's implementation of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The veteran politician also faulted the central government for failing to respect agreements despite his mediation efforts between the PML-N and the PTI-led KP government. Security details comprising police and Federal Constabulary personnel assigned to Fazl and his family in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan were withdrawn the previous week.

In a related development, Fazl's son and former federal communications minister, Asad Mahmood, received two consecutive summonses from the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) for November 10 and 14. The anti-graft watchdog called him over suspected irregularities in appointments at the Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. According to NAB sources, Asad failed to appear before the bureau despite being summoned twice.

stories.title: Crude Oil Prices Climb Amid Renewed Supply Disruption Concerns in Middle East
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices advanced on Thursday following reports of renewed attacks and security incidents in the Middle East that stoked fears of supply constraints. Brent crude futures increased by USD 1.53, or 1.62 percent, to reach USD 96.14 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose USD 1.20, or 1.43 percent, to USD 84.88. Market activity remained on edge ahead of the US Thanksgiving holiday, with traders reacting closely to geopolitical developments.

The upward pressure on prices followed statements from Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement claiming responsibility for strikes on Saudi Arabia’s primary oil refinery in Ras Tanura and Riyadh's financial district. Simultaneously, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz faced severe disruptions after Iran’s Revolutionary Guards reported that two tankers exploded and caught fire following strikes by sea mines near Oman’s Khasab port. These incidents threaten to stall the ongoing recovery of oil flows from the region.

Additional supply concerns emerged internationally, including production unit shutdowns at Thailand’s Phra Khanong oil refinery following a fire and serious damage inflicted by a drone attack on a Russian facility in the Krasnodar region. Meanwhile, official data showed that US crude inventories grew by 1.1 million barrels to reach 418.9 million barrels for the week ending November 20. OPEC+ ministers are scheduled to convene to review their upcoming output policy amidst ongoing discussions regarding production capacities and quotas.

stories.title: Euro Zone Bond Yields Rise as Global Equities and Oil Prices Recover
stories.summary:
Euro zone government bond yields increased on Thursday, breaking a four-session streak of declines as investors reduced their exposure to safe-haven assets. The shift was driven by a broader recovery in global equity markets and higher crude oil prices. Markets displayed minimal reaction to reports regarding the prospective nomination of Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos to lead the European Central Bank, with analysts anticipating that the institution will maintain its core focus on inflation and consensus-driven decision-making.

Germany's 10-year government bond yields climbed by 5 basis points to reach 3.266 percent, moving up from a multi-day low recorded the previous day. Equities gained ground as concerns regarding recent US tariff proposals eased, while the Thanksgiving holiday provided a temporary respite from volatility in the technology sector. Furthermore, European Central Bank data indicated that corporate lending growth reached its fastest pace in over three years, reflecting economic resilience against high energy costs.

German 2-year bond yields, which closely track policy rate expectations, rose by 6 basis points to 3.079 percent. Regarding the leadership transition at the central bank, EU officials indicated support for Spain's De Cos over Klaas Knot to succeed Christine Lagarde. Analysts noted that while De Cos previously held a dovish stance while heading the Bank of Spain, future policy direction will likely be shaped by broader economic conditions.

stories.title: امریکہ میں پاکستانی سفیر کا پاک ایران تنازع پر بیان
stories.summary:
امریکہ میں تعینات پاکستان کے سفیر رضوان سعید شیخ نے کہا ہے کہ پاکستان نے امریکہ اور ایران کے درمیان تنازع کے دوران ایک قابلِ اعتماد ثالث کا اہم سیاسی کردار ادا کیا ہے۔ انہوں نے یہ بات امریکہ میں یومِ شکر گزاری کے موقع پر اپنے ایک پیغام میں کہی، جس میں دوطرفہ تعلقات اور عالمی امور پر گفتگو کی گئی۔

سفیر پاکستان نے اپنے بیان میں مزید کہا کہ پاکستان آنے والے وقتوں میں بھی دنیا بھر میں امن و خوشحالی کے فروغ اور مختلف تنازعات کے پرامن حل کے لیے اپنی تعمیری خدمات پیش کرتا رہے گا۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ گزشتہ ایک سال کے دوران دونوں ممالک کے درمیان شراکت داری اور تعلقات میں مزید استحکام آیا ہے، جو کہ انتہائی لائقِ تحسین ہے۔

اس موقع پر دوطرفہ تعلقات کی اہمیت پر زور دیا گیا اور علاقائی امن کے قیام کے لیے سفارتی کوششوں کو جاری رکھنے کے عزم کا اعادہ کیا گیا۔ سفیر پاکستان کے اس بیان سے عالمی سطح پر ملک کے مثبت کردار اور امن دشمن عناصر کے خلاف کی جانے والی کوششوں کو اجاگر کیا گیا ہے۔
