stories.title: US Announces Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners to Counter Capacity
stories.summary:
The United States government unveiled a new series of proposed tariffs targeting imports from 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union, in a coordinated effort to counter excessive industrial capacity. Announced by the Office of the US Trade Representative, the levies are structured under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, providing a firmer legal foundation after the US Supreme Court struck down previous broad global duties enacted under emergency powers in February.

Under the new proposals, China faces the highest rate at 20%, which aligns with an existing trade truce set to expire on January 10. Should Beijing and Washington fail to extend the agreement, China's tariff rate could escalate to 40%. Other nations face conditional rates tied to ongoing negotiations, such as India at 17% or 25% and Vietnam at 20% or 35% depending on whether trade deals are finalized. Additionally, Brazil faces a 10% duty on finished aircraft due to unaddressed trade practices, while caps are established at 18% for several Southeast Asian nations and 15% for entities including Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, and the EU.

The announcement follows the Republican Party's midterm election setbacks and precedes a public hearing scheduled for January 25, after which the measures will take effect. Financial markets in Asia and Europe responded positively on Thursday, showing minimal disruption as the tariff adjustments were largely anticipated by economic analysts.

stories.title: Shaheen Afridi Claims Seven Wickets as FATA Secures Lead
stories.summary:
Pakistan ODI captain Shaheen Shah Afridi delivered a stellar bowling performance on Thursday, claiming seven wickets for 43 runs to help bundle out Faisalabad for 156 on the opening day of the fifth round of the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold at the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi. Shaheen's figures brought his tournament tally to 26 wickets across four matches, encompassing two five-wicket hauls and a pair of four-wicket outings. Faisalabad's innings was anchored by Faheem Ashraf, who scored 71 runs before FATA responded with a first-innings total of 176 in 34.4 overs, propelled by Mohammad Farooq's 90-run knock and 34 runs from Shaheen, securing a 20-run lead.

Elsewhere in the country, the opening day of the round featured other notable bowling and batting displays. At the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium, Test spinner Abrar Ahmed took five wickets for 21 runs and left-arm paceman Mir Hamza claimed four for 28 to dismiss Lahore Whites for 123. Karachi Blues capitalized by finishing the day at 132 without loss, with Abdullah Fazal unbeaten on 63 and Mohammad Taha on 55, giving their team a nine-run advantage.

In Islamabad at the National Ground, Raja Hamza Waheed contributed 73 runs and Mohammad Wasim Junior remained not out on 46 to push Islamabad to 277 for seven against Sialkot Blues. Meanwhile, at the Diamond Cricket Ground in Peshawar, Niaz Khan reinforced his status as the tournament's leading wicket-taker as Peshawar Blues closed strongly at 153 for two, holding a 45-run lead over Multan.

stories.title: گجرات میں بڑی بہن کو زہر دے کر قتل کرنے والی چھوٹی بہن اور اس کا دوست گرفتار
stories.summary:
پنجاب کے شہر گجرات میں پولیس نے 21 سالہ لڑکی کو اپنی ہی بڑی بہن کے قتل کے الزام میں گرفتار کر لیا ہے۔ پولیس کے مطابق ملزمہ نے اپنے تعلقات چھپانے کی غرض سے بڑی بہن کو زہر آلود نوڈلز کھلانے کے بعد گلہ گھونٹ کر مار ڈالا، اور اس واقعے میں ملوث اس کے ایک دوست کو بھی گرفتار کر لیا گیا ہے۔

واقعہ 17 نومبر کو پیش آیا جب لڑکیوں کے والدین گھر پر موجود نہیں تھے۔ والد کے اسپتال سے واپس آنے پر دونوں بیٹیوں نے زہریلے نوڈلز کھانے کا بتایا، جنہیں تشویشناک حالت میں ہسپتال لے جایا گیا جہاں بڑی بیٹی جاں بحق ہو گئی جبکہ چھوٹی بیٹی زیر علاج رہی۔ پولیس نے شک کی بنیاد پر پوسٹ مارٹم کروایا جس سے انکشاف ہوا کہ موت زہر اور گلا دبانے سے ہوئی۔

صحتیاب ہونے کے بعد چھوٹی بہن نے اعتراف کیا کہ اس نے اپنے ایک دوست سے تعلقات چھپانے کے لیے نوڈلز میں زہر ملایا تھا اور واقعے کو حادثہ ظاہر کرنے کے لیے خود بھی ایک چمچ کھایا تھا۔ بعد ازاں دونوں ملزمان نے زبردستی بڑی بہن کو زہریلے نوڈلز کھلائے اور موت یقینی بنانے کے لیے اس کا گلا دبا دیا۔

مقتولہ کے والد کی مدعیت میں 25 نومبر کو باقاعدہ ایف آئی آر درج کی گئی جس میں قتل کی دفعات شامل ہیں۔ تفتیشی افسر کے مطابق مقتولہ نے اپنی چھوٹی بہن کو تعلق ختم کرنے کا کہا تھا ورنہ والدین کو بتانے کی دھمکی دی تھی، جبکہ جیو فینسنگ سے بھی مرد ملزم کی وقوعے کے وقت موجودگی کے شواہد ملے ہیں۔

stories.title: Elon Musk Pledges Two SpaceX Shares for Every American Child
stories.summary:
Elon Musk announced on Wednesday that every child in the United States will receive two shares in SpaceX, his space and artificial intelligence company, in a pledge valued at approximately $18 billion. Musk stated that children will receive one share directly from the company and a second share from him personally. According to SpaceX, the corporate share will be contributed to every active Trump Account, a federal program designed to help Americans under the age of 18 build wealth and gain an early stake in the stock market. White House figures from October indicated that nearly 70 million Trump Accounts have been opened.

Detailing the timeline of the transfers, SpaceX stated that its newly issued Class A common stock share will be transferred next month, while Musk noted his personal share transfer will occur after his lockup period expires in June of next year. Based on SpaceX shares closing at $127.44 on Wednesday, the total pledge reaches nearly $18 billion. Financial analysts noted that the initiative builds a massive, long-term retail shareholder base and engages younger generations directly with the stock market as they come of age. Musk, whose net worth is estimated at around $824 billion, previously held roughly 6.42 billion shares in the company as of June.

The announcement comes amid growing public and political scrutiny over wealth distribution during the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. Competitor AI company Anthropic recently committed 5 percent of its shares, worth approximately $54 billion, to a public good fund. Other prominent billionaires have also engaged in large-scale philanthropy, including Warren Buffett, who has reportedly given away $60 billion, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, which has distributed over $100 billion since 2000.

stories.title: پاکستانی خلا باز ذیشان علی نے چین کے خلائی سٹیشن پر قدم رکھا
stories.summary:
چین کے انسان بردار خلائی مشن شینژو 24 کے ذریعے پاکستانی پائلٹ محمد ذیشان علی نے خلا کا تاریخی سفر مکمل کرتے ہوئے چین کے تیانگونگ خلائی سٹیشن میں داخل ہو گئے ہیں۔ اس مشن میں کمانڈر تانگ ہونگ بو اور فلائٹ انجینیئر وو یی بھی شامل ہیں، جب کہ محمد ذیشان علی بطور پے لوڈ سپیشلسٹ اس مشن کا حصہ بنے ہیں۔ اس طرح ذیشان علی خلا کا سفر کرنے والے پہلے پاکستانی اور چین کے خلائی سٹیشن تک پہنچنے والے پہلے غیر ملکی خلا باز بن گئے ہیں۔

اس تاریخی مشن کے دوران پاکستانی خلا باز کی خوراک اور ثقافتی ترجیحات کا خاص خیال رکھا گیا ہے۔ چینی سرکاری چینل سی جی ٹی این کے مطابق تیانگونگ خلائی سٹیشن پر چھ افراد کے لیے تیار کردہ خصوصی حلال مینیو میں ایک سو سے زائد پاکستانی اور روایتی پکوان شامل کیے گئے ہیں۔ ان کھانوں میں بیف نہاری، لیمب قورمہ، بثر چکن اور چنے کا سالن نمایاں طور پر شامل ہیں، جنہیں دیکھ کر سوشل میڈیا پر صارفین نے حیرت، خوشی اور پاک چین دوستی کے حوالے سے بھرپور تبصرے کیے ہیں۔

خلائی تحقیقاتی ادارے سپارکو اور چائنا مینڈ سپیس ایجنسی کے اشتراک سے ہونے والے اس منصوبے کے تحت محمد ذیشان علی خلائی سٹیشن پر تقریباً ایک ہفتہ یعنی چھ روز قیام کریں گے۔ اس مختصر مدت کے دوران وہ مائیکرو گریویٹی کے ماحول میں میٹریل سائنس، فلوئیڈ فزکس، حیاتیاتی علوم اور بائیوٹیکنالوجی سے متعلق سائنسی تجربات سر انجام دیں گے۔ ان تجربات میں خلائی ماحول میں مائیکرو الجی کی افزائش اور کوئنوا کے بیجوں پر کائناتی شعاعوں کے اثرات کا مطالعہ شامل ہے۔

یہ تمام سائنسی تجربات پاکستانی جامعات اور محققین کے تعاون سے تیار کیے گئے ہیں، جن کا مقصد مستقبل کے طویل مدتی خلائی مشنز کے لیے خوراک اور آکسیجن کے ذرائع تلاش کرنا اور موسمیاتی تبدیلیوں و غذائی تحفظ میں بہتری لانا ہے۔ اس اہم کامیابی کو پاکستان کی خلائی تحقیق کی تاریخ میں ایک بڑا سنگِ میل قرار دیا جا رہا ہے، جس نے بین الاقوامی سطح پر بھی خاصی توجہ حاصل کی ہے۔

stories.title: Global Events and Trends Expected to Shape the Year 2027
stories.summary:
The year 2027 is projected to bring several major global developments, including a powerful El Nino weather pattern, a shifting US Congress, and a high-stakes French presidential election. According to United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization official Kaveh Zahedi, the intense El Nino cycle could break global temperature records, exacerbating climate change and threatening agricultural harvests and food prices already strained by reduced global aid and the war in Iran.

In the United States, a Democratic takeover of both congressional chambers following the November midterms will reshape the final two years of President Donald Trump's term. Set to be overseen by incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic majority plans to push for lowered living costs, the rollback of tariffs, and potential investigations and subpoenas. However, sweeping legislative changes will face high hurdles due to presidential veto powers and narrow Senate margins.

In Europe, French President Emmanuel Macron will step down following the presidential election scheduled for April 18 and May 2. Amid deep societal divisions and protests, far-right figure Marine Le Pen and radical-left leader Jean-In-Mel Melenchon lead the polls, while other parties discuss primaries to narrow a diverse field of hopefuls requiring 500 elected official endorsements.

Additionally, a total solar eclipse will occur on August 2, offering up to six minutes of darkness visible across the far south of Spain, North Africa, and the Middle East, particularly near the Egyptian Pyramids. In sports, Brazil will host the Women's World Cup, where reigning champions Spain, England, and the United States will compete for the title at the Maracana Stadium.

These upcoming milestones highlight a diverse array of political, environmental, and cultural shifts across the globe. Observers and leaders alike are preparing for the significant disruptions and opportunities these anticipated events will bring to international stability and domestic policies.

stories.title: Fuel Truck Crash and Subsequent Fire Leave Thirty-One Dead in Cairo
stories.summary:
A devastating fire broke out in the Egyptian capital of Cairo on Wednesday, resulting in the deaths of at least 31 people after a fuel truck overturned on a busy highway. The incident occurred on the Ring Road in the densely populated Al-Waraq neighborhood of the Giza Governorate, engulfing nearby vehicles in a massive fireball and thick black smoke.

In response to the emergency, the health ministry dispatched 39 ambulances to the scene and transported 15 injured individuals to hospitals, with four listed in critical condition. Egypt's public prosecutor initiated an investigation into the disaster, utilizing DNA testing to identify victims who suffered severe burns. Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar traveled to the site and nearby medical facilities as the government elevated its emergency alert status.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly ordered a full inquiry to determine the causes of the accident and assess future transport safety measures for petroleum products. Authorities confirmed that the Ring Road has since been cleared and reopened to traffic following the removal of the charred wreckage.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar issued formal statements expressing deep grief and offering heartfelt condolences to President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, the bereaved families, and the people of Egypt. They reaffirmed Pakistan's solidarity during this tragic time.

The disaster highlights ongoing concerns regarding infrastructure and transit safety in Egypt, where informal urban areas and frequent traffic accidents claim thousands of lives annually. State statistics previously reported nearly 6,000 road deaths in the country over the past year.

stories.title: Slain Palestinian Journalist Mariam Dagga Posthumously Awarded Rory Peck Prize
stories.summary:
Palestinian war correspondent Mariam Dagga, who died in an Israeli air strike in Gaza last year, has been posthumously awarded the prestigious Rory Peck prize for freelance video journalists. The announcement was made in London on Wednesday by the Rory Peck Trust, recognizing her courageous documentation of the ongoing conflict alongside her colleagues.

Dagga shares the honor with Associated Press colleagues Abdel Kareem Hana and Jehad Alshrafi for their powerful coverage of the human cost of the war. Dagga was 33 years old when she was killed in August 2025 during an Israeli strike on a southern Gaza hospital that also claimed the lives of four other journalists. Associated Press executive editor Julie Pace praised the essential role journalists play in informing the public despite immense personal risks.

During the London ceremony, French photographer Robin Tutenges also received the inaugural Rory Peck Award for Photojournalism for his work in Ethiopia's Amhara region. Meanwhile, Sudanese freelance photographer Ahmed Mohamed Abdalla was shortlisted for his coverage of El-Fasher's fall in Sudan's civil war, though he could not attend after the UK government denied his visa.

The Rory Peck Trust has presented the award annually since 1995 to celebrate the work of freelance video journalists, commemorating video journalist Rory Peck who was killed in Moscow in 1993.

The international recognition underscores the extreme dangers faced by media workers reporting from active conflict zones around the world, particularly in Gaza and Sudan.

stories.title: India Aims for Christchurch Victory to Revive World Test Championship Hopes
stories.summary:
India is targeting a decisive victory in the second and final Test match against New Zealand in Christchurch to reignite their World Test Championship campaign after a frustrating draw in Wellington. Despite dominating large portions of the series opener on a placid wicket, India was unable to bowl out New Zealand in the second innings, leaving them in fourth place in the standings.

Shubman Gill’s squad faces a challenging path, needing victories in all six of their remaining matches in the current cycle, including five home fixtures against Australia. Bowling coach Morne Morkel emphasized that the team must focus on solving immediate cricketing challenges rather than overwhelming themselves with the pressure of reaching the final. India previously finished as runners-up to New Zealand in the inaugural WTC final in 2021.

In the opening Test, India batted strongly, with six of their top seven batters scoring over 50 runs before declaring at 720-9. Pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah returned impressively after a year-long absence, though the bowling attack ultimately fell five wickets short of victory. New Zealand slipped to third in the WTC table following the draw, which included twin failures from captain Tom Latham.

For the upcoming match in Christchurch, New Zealand fast bowler Matt Henry anticipates varied conditions at his home ground, noting that pitches typically flatten out after offering early bounce. The Black Caps enter the fixture without Tim Tickner, who was ruled out due to a hamstring injury sustained earlier in the series.

Both teams are heavily relying on their pace attacks as they prepare for the crucial showdown. The outcome in Christchurch will heavily influence the race for the top two spots in the World Test Championship standings ahead of next year's final.

stories.title: US Imposes New Tariffs on China to Reshape Global Trade
stories.summary:
The United States has introduced new tariff hikes on China, increasing levies by approximately 20% on top of existing 25% duties from the first Trump administration. The measures aim to pressure Beijing over unfair industrial practices and excess global capacity, while reordering international trade dynamics. Although the changes fall within a current trade truce, they provide Washington with leverage ahead of an upcoming leaders' summit in Miami and the January 10 expiration of the current trade pact.

China's foreign ministry has rejected allegations of unfair industrial policies but has refrained from issuing immediate retaliatory threats. Meanwhile, Beijing has extended a suspension on rare earth export controls and secured an aircraft purchase deal involving Xiamen Airlines and Boeing. Economists note that while Washington seeks to shrink its trade deficit with Beijing and curb excess Chinese manufacturing supply, policymakers remain wary of potential inflationary impacts that could trouble voters, particularly following congressional midterm election results.

The broader US trade strategy also involves scrutinizing other economies, such as the European Union and Vietnam, over their trade ties and investment inflows from China. Analysts point out that Beijing's ongoing struggle to restructure its domestic economy and stimulate household consumption continues to drive international trade friction. As Brussels and other global partners pursue separate trade measures and quotas, both Washington and Beijing are under pressure to navigate future negotiations carefully to avoid another full-scale trade war.

stories.title: Security Forces Eliminate 12 Terrorists Across Balochistan Districts
stories.summary:
Pakistani security forces killed 12 terrorists during a series of intelligence-based operations conducted across four districts of Balochistan between November 20 and 23. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, the counterterrorism actions took place in the Nushki, Sevi, Panjgur, and Kech districts as part of the ongoing "Azm-e-Istehkam" campaign. Eight individuals were killed during a hideout raid in Nushki, while subsequent operations in Sevi, Panjgur, and Kech accounted for the remaining casualties alongside the recovery of weapons and ammunition.

The military's media wing identified the slain individuals as members of Fitna al-Hindustan, alleging they received backing from India. President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised the security forces for successfully targeting terrorist hideouts and executing the operations. Both leaders emphasized the government's strong resolve to eradicate foreign-sponsored terrorism and maintain peace and stability throughout the country.

The high-level commendations underscore the state's continued focus on neutralizing militant elements within Balochistan. Authorities reiterated that counterterrorism measures will persist across all regions of Pakistan to dismantle networks attempting to disrupt regional development and security. Officials confirmed that the sacrifices made by security personnel will be supported by the entire nation in the ongoing fight against insurgency.

stories.title: Senior JUI-F Leaders Detained in Sargodha Amid Ongoing Political Tensions
stories.summary:
Several senior leaders of the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl, including National Assembly member Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, were detained by police in Sargodha late Wednesday. Regional Police Officer Sohail Sukhera stated that Haideri, along with party figures Malik Awais and Maulana Amjad Khan, had their movements restricted and were served notices for violating Section 144 across the division. In a separate operation in Khushab district, police registered a first information report against multiple local JUI-F members under various penal code sections and the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance for holding an unauthorized rally.

The party vehemently condemned the detentions and called for the immediate release of its leaders. JUI-F spokesperson Aslam Ghouri criticized the Punjab government for arresting officials without warrants and questioned why opposition gatherings were banned when provincial leadership held rallies. The detentions follow a period of heightened friction between JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and the federal government, stemming from disagreements over governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and alleged state restrictions on the party leadership's movements and security details.

Tensions have further escalated amid political fallout involving opposition and coalition figures. While PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has voiced support for Fazl and condemned government actions against him, the JUI-F has faced mounting pressure, including National Accountability Bureau summonses directed at the party chief's son regarding past public sector appointments. JUI-F has previously staged protests in Sindh and Balochistan to denounce what it terms a coordinated character assassination campaign against its leadership.

stories.title: PIA UK Flights Disrupted After Norse Atlantic Suspends Aircraft Lease
stories.summary:
Pakistan International Airlines experienced significant disruption to its United Kingdom flight operations after Norwegian carrier Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended a wet-lease agreement for two aircraft. The unexpected withdrawal occurred without prior notice just as passenger check-in was commencing, forcing the cancellation of scheduled flight PK 786 from London to Islamabad and flight PK 710 from Manchester to Lahore.

In response to the sudden shortage of leased aircraft and operational challenges, PIA announced alternative arrangements to stabilize its schedule. The airline stated it would deploy its own Boeing 777 aircraft to maintain UK services starting November 26, effectively reducing its reliance on third-party providers. Management apologized to affected travelers and initiated efforts to contact passengers for transfer to alternative flights while advising customers to verify their status online or through the call centre before heading to the airport.

stories.title: Sindh Chief Minister Suspends Key Officials Following Karachi Building Collapse
stories.summary:
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah ordered the suspension of several high-ranking administration and police figures on Thursday following a fatal building collapse in Karachi. The incident occurred at a newly constructed site within the Karachi Administration Employees Cooperative Housing Society near the Baloch Colony flyover. Among those removed from their posts are the Secretary of Local Government and Town Planning Sindh, along with Dr. Waseem Shamshad Ali, who served as Director General of the Sindh Building Control Authority. Furthermore, the chief minister dismissed Deputy Commissioner East Nasrullah Abbasi and Senior Superintendent of Police East Zubair Nazir Sheikh due to severe supervisory negligence.

The administrative actions were finalized during a specialized meeting called by the chief minister to address the disaster. In addition to the senior leadership terminations, Murad Ali Shah instructed federal authorities to suspend Dr. Waseem Shamshad Ali and launch a formal inquiry against him. Directives were also issued for the immediate suspension of 16 other relevant officials from the building control authority. Authorities were ordered to detain the property owner, Salman Tahir, alongside the builder, Zeeshan Aslam, who is also known as Shani. Meanwhile, the chief secretary was instructed to incorporate the project's architect and engineer into the ongoing investigation to ascertain culpability regarding violations of official building blueprints.

The structural failure befell a ground-plus-six-storey structure complete with a penthouse, which had been erected on a 600-square-yard plot. Official records from the building control authority indicate that the approved blueprint permitted merely a ground-plus-one-storey layout. Construction filings also linked Muhammad Abdullah Shakeel, Bilal Shakeel, and architect Muhammad Farhan Baseer to the development. The catastrophic event transpired on Wednesday while numerous laborers and workers remained inside, sparking a massive search and rescue operation that persisted through Thursday.

Emergency responders recovered three deceased victims while 14 others sustained injuries, and 17 individuals remain unaccounted for underneath the heavy debris. Distraught relatives spent the night outdoors at the catastrophe zone, sitting directly on pathways while managing their own hydration needs due to an absence of basic amenities. Concurrently, the Sindh High Court on Thursday reserved its final verdict concerning a petition filed by Dr. Nazish Butt from the Jinnah Sindh Medical University, which challenged a previous ruling by the federal ombudsman regarding a workplace harassment case.

stories.title: Unbeaten Pakistan Shaheens Prepare for Asia Cup Rising Stars Semifinal
stories.summary:
The defending champions, the Pakistan Shaheens, are gearing up to face Bangladesh 'A' in the semi-final of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars on Friday. Led by captain Abdul Samad, the team enters the knockout stage as favorites after securing victories in all three of their Group B matches. During a training session in Doha, Samad noted that the team aims to address earlier group-stage mistakes, bat for the full 50 overs, and rely on their strong bowling attack to defend targets.

Throughout the group stage at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha, the Shaheens recorded a 61-run win over the United Arab Emirates, defeated arch-rivals India 'A' by 48 runs, and beat Nepal by 96 runs. Opening batter Maaz Sadaqat leads the squad with 125 runs, while Hasan Nawaz has contributed 114 runs and earned a player-of-the-match award against India 'A'. In the bowling department, left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim has taken seven wickets, and fast bowler Ali Raza has claimed six.

The 15-member squad is managed and coached by former Pakistan batter Ijaz Ahmed Junior, alongside support staff including Riffatullah Mohmand, Rehan Riaz, Asfandyar Khan, Aleem Bajwa, and Zubair Ahmed. The upcoming semi-final match is scheduled with the toss at 2:30 pm Pakistan time and the first ball at 3 pm. The winner of this clash will advance to the final, which is set to take place on November 29 at the same venue.

stories.title: Grace Brassel Details Alleged Cruel Behaviour by Ex-Partner Shane Gillis
stories.summary:
Grace Brassel has publicly shared her experience of dating comedian Shane Gillis in a newly published essay for The Cut. The former couple was together for slightly over a year, from May 2024 to August 2025, after Brassel initially reached out to Gillis following his Netflix series Tires. Their romance began with trips to Austin, Texas, and eventually led to living together in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and Austin.

In her essay, Brassel detailed a shift in the dynamic once they shared a household. She stated that Gillis expected her to handle cooking and cleaning duties, while criticizing her behavior and wardrobe. According to Brassel, he frequently used severe remarks disguised as jokes and told her she was not 'being good' when things did not suit him. She stated that the relationship ended in July 2025 after she discovered he was cheating on her while using his phone to play music.

Responding to The Cut, Gillis remarked that they had good times together and wished her the best. The essay follows public backlash earlier this year when Gillis hosted Saturday Night Live and made a controversial monologue joking about women's gym attire. In response to those remarks, Brassel shared workout content on her Instagram account, addressing the comments through a fitness routine and outfit check.

stories.title: Japan's Nikkei Recovers Sharply as Investors Buy Artificial Intelligence Dips
stories.summary:
Japan's primary stock index experienced a significant rebound on Thursday, recovering from near multi-month lows as market participants capitalized on recent price drops by purchasing artificial intelligence-focused equities. The tech-heavy Nikkei share average advanced 1.6 percent to reach 57,902.41 points by early trading, following an even steeper intraday surge exceeding two percent. This upward movement arrived directly after the index plunged to 56,502.97 on Wednesday, hovering closely above the previous Friday's trough of 56,436.65, which marked its weakest positioning since April 13.

Individual technology names recorded substantial gains during the session, led by chipmaker Kioxia Holdings, which soared 12.1 percent to become the benchmark index's top percentage gainer. This sharp recovery followed a dramatic 14 percent decline on Wednesday that had pushed the stock to an eight-month low. Similarly, artificial intelligence startup investor SoftBank Group appreciated by more than 10 percent after dropping nearly 15 percent in the prior session to its lowest valuation since July of the previous year. Advantest, a major chip-testing equipment manufacturer, climbed 6.3 percent and contributed 324 points to the broader index's total gain of 890 points.

Despite the positive daily momentum, market strategists cautioned that the sector remains prone to turbulence. Wataru Akiyama, a strategist at Nomura Securities, noted that artificial intelligence-related equities will likely exhibit continued stop-and-go trading behavior, characterized by dip-buying during market corrections and subsequent sell-offs once recoveries reach specific thresholds. Akiyama emphasized that underlying anxieties concerning the long-term financial viability of infrastructure investments in the technology sector have not been fully alleviated by the latest market bounce.

The broader market has fluctuated heavily throughout the week, driven by executive leadership changes at artificial intelligence bellwether Nvidia and investor concerns that a Democratic victory in recent United States midterm elections might impede infrastructure development. Market breadth on Thursday remained positive, with 185 components of the Nikkei advancing, 38 declining, and two remaining unchanged. Trading activity across Asia and global financial markets continues to monitor macroeconomic indicators, currency fluctuations, and shifting commodity prices closely amid ongoing economic developments.

stories.title: Australian Dollar Gains on Data Center Investments While Kiwi Holds Steady
stories.summary:
The Australian dollar strengthened on Thursday, bolstered by robust business investment figures centered heavily around the construction of new data centers. This positive economic momentum followed a turbulent preceding session where the currency fluctuated alongside international equities. Meanwhile, the New Zealand dollar demonstrated resilience, maintaining its position away from a 17-year low amid broader global financial market volatility. The Australian currency climbed 0.2 percent to trade at $0.6638, recovering after it slipped to a fresh one-year low of $0.6559 earlier in the week.

Official data released on Thursday indicated that Australian business investment expanded significantly during the September quarter, marking the sharpest quarterly increase since the peak of the national mining boom in 2011. Corporate entities funneled substantial capital into data facilities, though a large portion of this expenditure was directed toward imported equipment, which mitigates its direct impact on domestic economic growth. Furthermore, corporate surveys revealed that businesses have upgraded their capital expenditure forecasts for the near future. Harry McAuley, an economist at Oxford Economics Australia, projected that sector spending could expand from roughly 20 billion Australian dollars currently to approximately 60 billion Australian dollars annually by the year 2030.

Despite the strong investment indicators, financial markets continue to anticipate that the Reserve Bank of Australia's next policy adjustment will involve an interest rate reduction, though market pricing does not fully incorporate a rate cut until August, with an 83 percent probability currently assigned to a move by June. Australian government bond futures for the three-year tenor remained relatively flat at 95.54 after touching a five-month peak earlier in the session. Across the Tasman Sea, market swaps indicated an 80 percent likelihood that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand will implement a quarter-percentage-point interest rate increase to 3 percent.

The strengthening domestic data also influenced cross-rate valuations, as the Australian dollar advanced 0.2 percent against its New Zealand counterpart to reach 1.2100 New Zealand dollars. This recovery helped the Australian currency move away from a multi-month low touched earlier in the week, though it remains below its 13-year peak recorded in October. Analysts note that leading indicators continue to show numerous new projects breaking ground, supporting the economic outlook through the coming years despite near-term volatility in global currency markets.

stories.title: Singapore Urges US to Reconsider New Tariffs on Its Economy
stories.summary:
Singapore expressed deep disappointment on Thursday regarding newly proposed United States tariffs, stating the decision ignores the unique structure of its economy. The Energy, Trade and Industry Ministry announced its disagreement with the US Trade Representative's maximum potential tariff rate of 20%, which could be adjusted to 10% through a reciprocal trade agreement. Government officials emphasized that Singapore operates as an outward- and market-oriented global trading hub, meaning its global trade surplus reflects this structural role rather than domestic market protection or export subsidies. 

 Singapore highlighted that the US has maintained a consistent trade surplus with the nation for over two decades under their existing free trade agreement. The new tariffs emerged following an eight-month unfair trade practices investigation into excess industrial capacity. This move forms part of an administration effort to rebuild tariff leverage for President Donald Trump after the Supreme Court invalidated broad global duties in February. 

 As a small country with limited resources, Singapore relies on competing globally. The ministry noted that exports worth $7.4 billion are impacted by the measures and stated that authorities will investigate any potential tariff evasion while maintaining a realistic approach given the high volume of trade. 

 Despite its strong dissatisfaction, Singapore intends to continue constructive engagement with the USTR. Officials will urge Washington to reconsider the proposed actions and explore potential methods to reduce the tariff burden on the city-state.

stories.title: Civil Aviation Authority Permits PIA to Use Saudi Aircraft on Charter Basis
stories.summary:
The Civil Aviation Authority has granted Pakistan International Airlines permission to utilize aircraft operated by Saudi aviation operators on a charter basis. The measure aims to facilitate passenger transportation between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, specifically bringing travelers from Jeddah, Madinah, and other Saudi airports. 

 Sources within the CAA indicated that the authorization is valid for a 15-day period commencing on November 23. During these operations, the chartered aircraft will fly under the Saudi airline's specific call sign, SVA, while tickets for the flights will be booked exclusively through PIA. 

 The aviation regulator has mandated that PIA verify that all utilized aircraft possess valid airworthiness certificates and comprehensive insurance coverage. Upon landing in Pakistan, the chartered planes are required to complete mandatory safety inspections administered by the CAA. 

 Furthermore, PIA assumes total liability for any aircraft damage, passenger complaints, or accidents occurring throughout the charter operations. The CAA has also instructed the national carrier to finalize all associated contractual formalities promptly.

stories.title: Australian Legislation Permits Users to Opt Out of Social Media Algorithms
stories.summary:
Social media algorithms dictate online experiences by recommending content based on personal data and browsing habits, but new legislation in Australia will soon allow users to opt out of these features. Approved by the parliament, the upcoming rules will also penalize tech giants with fines if they fail to remove harmful material. Platforms such as TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and Reddit rely on these recommendation systems to predict user engagement, keeping codebases closely guarded as proprietary trade secrets. 

 Experts note that these features are engineered to create addictive cycles, frequently keeping both children and adults online past their intended limits at the cost of sleep and real-world connection. Mark Williams, an honorary professor of cognitive neuroscience at Macquarie University, pointed out that mechanisms like endless feeds and intermittent rewards trigger the dopamine system. Research published in Cureus last year likened this digital dependence to substance addiction, while specialists warn that algorithms prioritize provocative or extreme content because outrage drives user engagement and corporate profit. 

 In addition to the opt-out mechanism, the new Australian regulations require technology firms to protect minors under 18 from online bullying, pornography, and content that promotes crime or eating disorders. The initiative aims to return feeds to a basic chronological format centered on updates from friends, family, and followed pages. 

 However, academic experts question how widely the opt-out feature will be utilized by the public. A 2025 survey across six countries indicated that only one in five individuals would disable personalized recommendations, with researchers noting that the algorithms remain highly effective at holding user attention.

stories.title: Copper Prices Recover Past $12,000 Amid Easing US Tariff Fears
stories.summary:
Copper prices staged a recovery above $12,000 a metric ton on Thursday following two consecutive sessions of steep market selloffs. The rebound was supported by a recovery in Asian share markets, less severe US tariff proposals than initially feared, and a weakening US dollar. Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange advanced 2.65% to $11,958 per metric ton after peaking at $12,089. Meanwhile, the most-active copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange registered a minor decline of 0.07%, settling at 89,700 yuan or roughly $13,438 a ton. 

 The US administration unveiled proposed duties targeting goods from 14 major trading partners, including Japan, China, and the European Union, following an investigation into excess industrial capacity. Analysts noted that these proposed duties will not stack on top of tariffs imposed in July and are not anticipated to take effect until February or March. 

 Market sentiment had previously been dampened by artificial intelligence concerns, macroeconomic headwinds, and expectations of hawkish monetary policy. Analysts at Chinese brokerage Jinrui Futures suggested that the market had already largely priced in the impact of US tariffs, diminishing their future influence on trading activity. 

 A softer US dollar further aided metal prices by making greenback-priced commodities cheaper for international buyers using alternate currencies. Across other exchanges, LME metals including aluminium, zinc, lead, nickel, and tin also posted gains, while SHFE metals recorded mixed results.

stories.title: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari Calls for Political Reset Amid Economic Crisis
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has urged the country to pursue a political reset to confront severe economic challenges and regional geopolitical tensions. Speaking at a press conference at the Multan Press Club on Thursday, Bilawal described the current economic crisis as unprecedented in his lifetime. He emphasized that the rising cost of living is placing a heavy burden on citizens, making it difficult for ordinary people to cover basic expenses like transportation, meals, and healthcare.

Bilawal highlighted that system resilience requires inclusive democratic deliberations involving both government allies and opposition parties. He criticized the opposition for boycotting key parliamentary committees, such as those overseeing the judiciary and electoral reforms, arguing that transparent elections and public trust are essential for any stable government. He also stressed the importance of a free press to ensure accountability and help political leaders make informed decisions, noting that freedom of media is vital for a democratic reset.

Addressing past legislative efforts, Bilawal clarified his stance on constitutional amendments, stating that the 26th Amendment was achieved through extensive consensus with parties like the PTI and Maulana Fazlur Rehman. He emphasized that future amendments, including discussions around a potential 27th amendment, should similarly rely on broad agreement. He urged politicians and the media to focus directly on the economic struggles affecting the public rather than avoiding the core issues.

stories.title: Indian Government Bonds Slide Amid Oil Price Surge and Food Inflation Concerns
stories.summary:
Indian government bonds declined during early trading sessions, erasing previous gains as crude oil prices climbed past $95 per barrel. The downward pressure on bonds followed reports that Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, sparking supply disruption fears in the Middle East. Because India relies heavily on imported crude oil, sustained price increases threaten to expand the current account deficit, weaken the rupee, and drive up domestic inflation.

In addition to external energy pressures, the Reserve Bank of India highlighted persistent and broad-based food inflation across the country. According to a monthly bulletin from the central bank, high-frequency data from November 19 indicated strong price momentum with ongoing increases in major cereals and pulses. This suggested that price pressures extended well beyond a limited number of goods. Reports earlier in the month noted that weak monsoon rains tightened food supplies, while October retail inflation had already exceeded the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit.

Market participants and investors are monitoring the situation closely ahead of the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision scheduled for December 4. While a majority of economists surveyed by Reuters anticipate a 25 basis point rate hike, others are not discounting the possibility of more aggressive monetary action. Traders warned that persistent oil rallies and mounting inflation worries could completely reverse recent gains achieved in the country's bond market throughout the month.

stories.title: Chinese Equities Finish Flat Amid New US Tariff Proposals and Technology Concerns
stories.summary:
Chinese stocks ended a volatile trading session virtually unchanged as investors reacted to fresh trade proposals from the United States and lingering market anxieties surrounding artificial intelligence. The blue-chip CSI300 Index initially rose as much as 0.5% in morning trade, rebounding slightly from a 17-month low recorded in the prior session, before losing those gains by midday. Meanwhile, the Shanghai Composite Index remained relatively stable near 3,475.46, hovering close to its weakest levels since July 2025.

The market hesitation followed an announcement by US President Donald Trump regarding potential maximum tariffs ranging from 20% to 40% on fourteen major trading partners, including China. The proposed tariffs are intended to counteract excess industrial capacity promoted by these nations. A spokesperson representing the Chinese embassy in Washington formally rejected the characterization that China serves as a source of excess industrial capacity.

Domestic sector performance reflected the cautious investor sentiment, with the new-energy vehicle sector dropping by 0.7%. Battery manufacturer CATL experienced a significant decline, falling as much as 2.4% to reach a 26-month low, while the CSI Semiconductor Index fell by 1.5%. Conversely, Hong Kong markets performed better, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index climbing 1.9% to recover from lows not seen since April 2025, supported by a 2.6% increase in the Hang Seng Tech Index.

Analysts at Nanhua Futures noted that overall market sentiment remains downbeat. Global worries regarding artificial intelligence persist, and although local authorities introduced market-stabilization measures recently, their impact on investor confidence has been limited. Consequently, short-term stock indices are expected to maintain a weak trajectory as regional markets navigate ongoing macroeconomic and trade uncertainties.

stories.title: UK Contacts 100,000 Strategic Reservists Amid Heightened Defence Preparedness
stories.summary:
The UK Ministry of Defence has issued letters to approximately 100,000 strategic reservists, requesting that they prepare for a possible call-up. This marks the first time since the Cold War that such letters have been sent to this scale of reservists, offering opportunities to volunteer for training exercises. Signed by the heads of the Army, Navy, and Royal Air Force, the communications also ask individuals to provide updated contact details, current employment information, and skills.

The precautionary measure coincides with additional defence adjustments across British military bases. Reports indicate that the Royal Air Force has been storing aircraft in hangars overnight and planning anti-drone protections. These steps follow recent warnings from intelligence agency MI5 and the Ministry of Defence regarding elevated risks of Russian sabotage targeting British firms that supply Ukraine's military.

Defence officials have stressed the need for heightened readiness amid ongoing concerns regarding Europe's security and the Russia-Ukraine war. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has previously emphasized that Britain must prepare to fight and win alongside allies. Additionally, the government announced an £8 billion investment to enhance submarine readiness, while military leadership has warned the public that upcoming sacrifices may be required to prioritize national defence.

stories.title: Punjab Police Chief Directs Intensified Search Efforts for Disappeared Women Across Province
stories.summary:
Inspector General of Police Punjab, Rao Abdul Karim, chaired a dedicated review session to address the issue of disappeared women and directed law enforcement agencies to accelerate recovery operations. During the meeting, officials briefed the police chief that specialized investigative units, led by DIG-Investigation officers and comprising female police personnel, special branch agents, and investigators, have been established to tackle the crisis.

To strengthen ongoing investigations, the IG instructed officers to leverage national identity cards, B-forms, passports, mobile phone SIM cards, and travel histories. District Police Officers and Superintendents of Police were ordered to personally monitor daily progress on missing person files, paying close attention to current-year cases alongside older pending investigations. Furthermore, the police chief emphasized maintaining active communication with provincial police departments, prison authorities, and the Federal Investigation Agency.

The review follows a directive issued by the Lahore High Court, where Chief Justice Aalia Neelum heard a petition filed by a mother seeking the recovery of her missing daughter, Muqaddis. During the court proceedings, IG Rao Abdul Karim submitted a formal progress report regarding missing women cases. According to official police figures presented in court, over 100,000 cases of missing women were documented across Punjab between 2021 and 2025, with 387 cases remaining unresolved. Additionally, 21,956 cases were reported during the current year of 2026, out of which 1,781 cases are still pending resolution.

stories.title: Seventeen Still Missing Following Building Collapse in Karachi Housing Society
stories.summary:
Rescue operations continued after a newly constructed residential building collapsed in the Karachi Administration Employees Cooperative Housing Society near the Baloch Colony flyover. Authorities confirmed that three bodies have been recovered, 14 individuals sustained injuries, and 17 people remain unaccounted for following the incident, which occurred while numerous workers and labourers were inside the structure.

Families of the missing individuals spent the night at the collapse site under difficult conditions, waiting for news of their relatives. Distressed family members noted that the district administration provided inadequate facilities, pointing out that a designated facilitation tent contained only four chairs intended for the deputy commissioner's assistant commissioner, forcing grieving relatives to sit on the ground and footpaths.

Investigators and municipal records revealed that the collapsed structure was a ground-plus-six-storey building that included a penthouse built on a 600-square-yard plot, whereas the official approved building plan permitted only a ground-plus-one-storey layout. Sindh Building Control Authority records linked individuals including Muhammad Abdullah Shakeel, Bilal Shakeel, builder Zeeshan Aslam, and architect Muhammad Farhan Baseer to the project. In response to the disaster, Karachi Commissioner's spokesperson Sattar Javed announced that 12 other under-construction buildings in the area were sealed, and eight SBCA officials faced suspension. Meanwhile, rescue teams continued working through the rubble as families awaited updates on the missing workers.

stories.title: سابق پولیس اہلکار بیو لامارے سڈنی میں ڈبل قتل کا مجرم قرار
stories.summary:
آسٹریلیا کے شہر سڈنی کی عدالت نے فروری 2024 میں پیش آنے والے ایک ہولناک دوہرے قتل کے مقدمے کا فیصلہ سناتے ہوئے 31 سالہ سابق پولیس اہلکار بیو لامارے کو جیسی بیئرڈ اور اُن کے پارٹنر لیوک ڈیوس کے قتل کا مجرم قرار دے دیا ہے۔ اس مقدمے کی سماعت دو ماہ تک جاری رہی جس میں عدالت کو بتایا گیا کہ مجرم لامارے نے اپنے سرکاری پستول کا استعمال کرتے ہوئے اس سنگین واردات کو انجام دیا۔ مقتول جیسی بیئرڈ ماضی میں لامارے کے پارٹنر رہ چکے تھے۔

تحقیقات کے دوران یہ بات سامنے آئی کہ لامارے نے کئی ماہ پہلے ہی اس قتل کی باقاعدہ منصوبہ بندی شروع کر دی تھی۔ اس مقصد کے لیے انہوں نے ایک سرف بورڈ رکھنے والا بیگ خریدا جس میں بعد میں لاش کو چھپایا گیا، اس کے علاوہ ایک بارہ استعمال ہونے والا موبائل فون خریدا گیا اور جنگلات میں فائرنگ کی مشق بھی کی گئی۔ واردات کے روز مجرم نے اوبر ایٹس کے ڈیلیوری رائیڈر کا بھیس دھارا اور مقتول کے گھر کے باہر طویل وقت تک انتظار کرنے کے بعد گھر میں داخل ہوئے جہاں انہوں نے اس اندوہناک جرم کا ارتکاب کیا۔

مقدمے کے دوران استغاثہ نے سی سی ٹی وی فوٹیج اور متعدد گواہوں کے بیانات عدالت میں پیش کیے۔ گواہوں نے بتایا کہ لامارے نے قتل سے پہلے ان سے مشورے مانگے تھے اور بعد میں لاشوں کو ٹھکانے لگانے کے لیے مدد کی درخواست بھی کی تھی۔ دونوں مقتولین کی لاشیں بعد ازاں ایک دیہی علاقے سے لکڑیوں اور ملبے کے نیچے سے برآمد ہوئی تھیں جنہیں ایک فارم پر چھپانے کی کوشش کی گئی تھی۔

جیسی بیئرڈ اور لامارے کی ملاقات اکتوبر 2022 میں ہوئی تھی لیکن تعلق زیادہ عرصہ نہ چل سکا اور اپریل 2023 میں بیئرڈ نے تعلق ختم کر دیا۔ تاہم لامارے کا جنون اور غصہ بڑھتا گیا اور انا کو ٹھیس پہنچنے پر انہوں نے انتقامی کارروائی کا فیصلہ کیا۔ عدالتی فیصلے کے بعد متاثرہ خاندان کو انصاف کی امید ملی ہے جبکہ اس کیس نے سڈنی سمیت پورے ملک میں شدید ہلچل مچا دی تھی۔

stories.title: US President Trump Pursues New Tariffs Despite Midterm Setbacks
stories.summary:
United States President Donald Trump has advanced a new package of tariffs targeting 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan, and the European Union. The decision follows recent midterm elections where voters strongly blamed the administration's economic policies and tariffs for inflation and higher living costs. Exit polls conducted by SSRS revealed that two-thirds of voters believed tariffs harmed the national economy, while Yale University’s Budget Lab estimated the measures added $900 in annual household costs.

Despite the political backlash and a subsequent Supreme Court ruling striking down earlier duties as illegal in February, the Trump administration rolled out revised proposed rates ranging from 20% to 40% on targeted imports, which trade deals would generally constrain to between 10% and 20%. Chief trade negotiator Jamieson Greer announced the plan ahead of Thanksgiving. The policy revamps duties originally imposed in 2025 following an eight-month review of trade practices.

With Democrats securing control of Congress for the remaining two years of his term, analysts note that tariffs offer President Trump a crucial economic mechanism to project authority and pursue trade deficits without legislative approval. Supporters, including blue-collar labor groups like United Steelworkers International President Roxanne Brown, praised the action for protecting domestic workers and driving factory construction. Conversely, congressional critics, such as retiring Republican Representative Don Bacon, blamed the protectionist strategy for fueling inflation and depressing wage growth.

The announcement triggered immediate reactions across financial markets, with the benchmark S&P 500 falling a quarter of a percentage point. Democratic leaders swiftly condemned the move, arguing that the administration continues to ignore public anger over inflation and affordability. White House spokesman Matthew Middleton defended the initiative, asserting that ending lopsided trade agreements remains fundamental to the Make America Great Again movement and that the administration will persist in fighting to lower costs.

stories.title: ASEAN Plus Three Nations Agree to Link Digital Payment Systems
stories.summary:
Financial deputies and central bank governors from China, Japan, South Korea, and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations agreed during a meeting in Kyoto, Japan, to establish closer financial integration. The collaborative effort focuses on connecting domestic payment frameworks and harmonizing regulations for digital assets across regional borders. Officials emphasized that this initiative addresses the growing necessity for coordination as rapid digital transactions gain popularity throughout the region.

To manage these objectives, the ASEAN+3 grouping formed a dedicated working group. Furthermore, participants reviewed a newly implemented emergency lending mechanism designed to accelerate financial support during sudden economic shocks, such as natural disasters or pandemics. This mechanism functions as part of a revised agreement bolstering the region's $240-billion currency swap safety net, known as the Chiang Mai Initiative.

The comprehensive outcomes and specific details of the Kyoto discussions will be formally presented to finance ministers and central bank governors during their upcoming meeting in Nagoya, Japan, scheduled for May 2027. The ASEAN+3 coalition encompasses the 11 member nations of ASEAN alongside Japan, China, and South Korea, aiming to fortify regional economic stability and cross-border financial collaboration.

stories.title: South Waziristan Closes Schools in Wana and Azam Warsak
stories.summary:
Local authorities in South Waziristan ordered the closure of all public and private educational institutions in Wana and Azam Warsak for two days. The Deputy Commissioner issued the official notification, mandating closures on November 26 and 27 in response to deteriorating security conditions and public safety worries. The measure specifically aims to protect students and teachers whose schools are located near the SWS Camp.

The safety precautions follow a spike in local violence, notably an attack between November 24 and 25 where 12 strikes utilizing two quadcopter drones targeted Malik Khel Kallay in the Birmal tehsil of Lower South Waziristan within a single hour. Although the drone strikes caused property damage, no fatalities were reported, though the incident left residents in fear. Additional tension stems from an event on November 22 when unidentified motorcyclists shot and killed Police Constable Abdul Salam Dautani in Rustam Bazaar, Wana, near Mughal Khel Dairy.

In tandem with these localized security measures, the Pakistan Army and security forces have sustained intelligence-based operations throughout the region. Clashes and military actions in South Waziristan and neighboring districts during mid-November have resulted in the reported deaths of dozens of militants as authorities work to stabilize the area.

stories.title: Chinese Yuan Maintains Strength Near Three-Week High Despite Tariffs
stories.summary:
The Chinese yuan maintained a strong position near a three-week high against the United States dollar, showing resilience despite new tariff proposals from Washington and weaker central bank guidance. Spot yuan traded 0.07% firmer at 6.6636 per dollar, hovering near the peak reached during the previous session, while its offshore counterpart rose 0.09% to 6.6639 per dollar in Asian trading.

The currency's stability persists following US President Donald Trump's announcement of proposed maximum tariffs ranging from 20% to 40% on goods from major trading partners, including China, aimed at curbing alleged excess industrial capacity. Beijing's embassy spokesperson in Washington strongly rejected the excess capacity allegations. Meanwhile, the People’s Bank of China set its daily midpoint rate at 6.7096 per dollar, which was weaker than the previous session's four-year high and 441 pips lower than Reuters estimates.

Market analysts suggest the yuan's upward trajectory remains supported by ongoing trade negotiations and the managed nature of the currency's fixing mechanism. Experts at Goldman Sachs noted that while severe escalations in trade tensions could eventually stabilize the currency following recent gains, current policy implementation and prospective talks temper immediate downside risks. Concurrently, the broader dollar index slipped 0.1% to 103.81 as US equities pared losses, remaining well below the 19-month high recorded earlier in the week.

stories.title: Nvidia instructs partners to halt server shipments to Southeast Asian nations
stories.summary:
Nvidia has reportedly directed its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to four countries in Southeast Asia, according to a Financial Times report citing three knowledgeable sources. Manufacturing companies such as Dell and Supermicro informed buyers located in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia that the chipmaker is blocking their order deliveries.

The development comes as Nvidia and its partners attempt to navigate compliance requirements surrounding new United States export controls. At present, it remains unclear whether this shipping halt is a temporary measure while companies figure out how to adhere to the updated regulatory restrictions.

Major firms involved in the supply chain, including Nvidia, Dell, and Supermicro, did not provide immediate comments when contacted outside of regular business hours. The restriction affects regions that utilize these specialized servers packaged with Nvidia hardware for advanced computing workloads.

This shipping pause highlights ongoing international tensions and regulatory adjustments surrounding advanced technology trade. Industry stakeholders continue to monitor how these evolving US export policies will impact semiconductor distribution across global markets.

stories.title: Pakistan Maritime Minister urges seafood exporters to reach 5% value-added target
stories.summary:
Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry has called on local seafood exporters to ensure that at least five percent of their total shipments consist of value-added products. The minister highlighted that out of 578 registered seafood exporters in the country, only three currently engage in processing and value addition.

To address this gap and boost foreign exchange earnings, Chaudhry chaired a high-level meeting and established a dedicated committee. Headed by Fisheries Development Commissioner Dr Muhammad Hafeez-ur-Rehman, the committee includes representatives from provincial fisheries departments and the private sector to recommend practical ways to promote processed seafood.

During the discussions, officials reviewed strategies to diversify exports beyond raw commodities by improving packaging and processing capabilities. The minister advised businesses to initiate value-addition activities on a modest scale and gradually expand their operations to successfully penetrate higher-value international markets.

Additionally, the government plans to organize a stakeholder workshop to identify barriers and formulate actionable recommendations. Enhancing aquaculture infrastructure, such as shrimp hatcheries and modern processing plants, is viewed as vital to realizing Pakistan's true potential in the fisheries sector.

stories.title: کراچی میں عمارت گرنے کا واقعہ، وزیرِ اعلیٰ سندھ کا سخت ایکشن
stories.summary:
وزیراعلیٰ سندھ مراد علی شاہ نے کراچی کے علاقے ایڈمن سوسائٹی میں عمارت گرنے کے واقعے کا سخت نوٹس لیتے ہوئے اہم انتظامی شخصیات کو فوری طور پر ان کے عہدوں سے ہٹانے کا حکم دے دیا ہے۔ انہوں نے سیکریٹری بلدیات وسیم شمشاد کو ان کے عہدے کے ساتھ ساتھ ڈی جی ایس بی سی اے کے منصب سے بھی ہٹا دیا ہے جبکہ اس کے علاوہ غفلت برتنے پر ڈی سی ایسٹ نصراللہ عباسی اور ایس ایس پی ایسٹ زبیر شیخ کو بھی عہدے سے ہٹا دیا گیا ہے۔

اس سانحے کے بعد طلب کیے گئے ہنگامی اجلاس کے دوران وزیراعلیٰ سندھ نے سندھ بلڈنگ کنٹرول اتھارٹی کے 16 متعلقہ افسران کو بھی معطل کرنے کی ہدایات جاری کیں۔ حکام کا کہنا ہے کہ عمارت کے مالک اور بلڈر کو گرفتار کر لیا گیا ہے جبکہ اس واقعے کا مقدمہ ٹیپو سلطان تھانے میں سرکار کی مدعیت میں درج کر لیا گیا ہے۔ مقدمے میں مجموعی طور پر 10 افراد کو نامزد کیا گیا ہے جن میں سے چار نامزد ملزمان پولیس کی گرفت میں ہیں۔

مراد علی شاہ نے چیف سیکریٹری کو یہ بھی ہدایت کی ہے کہ حادثے کا شکار بننے والی عمارت کے آرکیٹیکٹ اور انجینئر کو بھی تفتیش کا حصہ بنایا جائے۔ اس کے علاوہ وفاقی حکومت کو سفارش کی گئی ہے کہ وسیم شمشاد کو معطل کر کے ان کے خلاف باقاعدہ انکوائری عمل میں لائی جائے۔ حکومت چاہتی ہے کہ اس حادثے کے ذمہ دار تمام افراد کو قانون کے کٹہرے میں لایا جائے۔

وزیراعلیٰ سندھ نے واضح کیا ہے کہ تفتیش کے دوران بلڈنگ کنٹرول اتھارٹی کا جو بھی ملازم یا افسر ملوث پایا گیا، اس کے خلاف سخت قانونی کارروائی کی جائے گی۔ انتظامیہ کی غفلت اور غیر قانونی تعمیرات کی وجہ سے پیش آنے والے اس واقعے کے بعد شہر بھر میں عمارتوں کے معیار اور حفاظتی اقدامات پر ایک بار پھر سوالیہ نشان لگ گئے ہیں۔

stories.title: کراچی کے علاقے بفر زون میں ڈکیتی، پولیس مقابلے میں دو ڈاکو ہلاک
stories.summary:
کراچی کے علاقے بفر زون سیکٹر 15 میں ایک گھر کے اندر ڈکیتی کی واردات کے دوران پولیس اور ملزمان کے درمیان شدید فائرنگ کا تبادلہ ہوا جس کے نتیجے میں دو ڈاکو موقع پر ہی ہلاک ہو گئے۔ پولیس حکام کے مطابق یہ واقعہ اس وقت پیش آیا جب چار مسلح ملزمان ایک رہائشی گھر میں گھس کر لوٹ مار کی کارروائی میں مصروف تھے اور موقع پر پولیس کی بروقت آمد ہوگئی۔

اطلاع ملتے ہی پولیس کی نفری فوری طور پر جائے وقوعہ پر پہنچ گئی، جس پر ملزمان نے وہاں سے فرار ہونے کی کوشش کی اور پولیس پارٹی پر فائرنگ شروع کر دی۔ پولیس کی جوابی کارروائی کے دوران دو ڈاکو گولیاں لگنے سے ہلاک ہو گئے جبکہ ان کے دو دیگر ساتھی موقع سے فرار ہونے میں کامیاب ہو گئے۔ پولیس اور سکیورٹی ادارے اب ان فرار ہونے والے ملزمان کی تلاش کے لیے چھاپے مار رہے ہیں۔

ابتدائی اطلاعات کے مطابق ہلاک ہونے والے ڈاکوؤں کے قبضے سے ایک گاڑی، گھر سے لوٹا ہوا قیمتی سامان اور غیر قانونی اسلحہ برآمد کر لیا گیا ہے۔ پولیس اس بات کی بھی تفتیش کر رہی ہے کہ آیا یہ گروہ شہر کے دیگر حصوں میں بھی اس طرح کی ڈکیتیوں اور سنگین وارداتوں میں ملوث رہا ہے یا نہیں۔

شہر میں بڑھتے ہوئے سٹریٹ کرائم اور گھروں میں ڈکیتی کی وارداتوں کے تناظر میں پولیس کی یہ کارروائی انتہائی اہمیت کی حامل قرار دی جا رہی ہے۔ قانون نافذ کرنے والے اداروں کا عزم ہے کہ شہریوں کے جان و مال کے تحفظ کو یقینی بنانے کے لیے جرائم پیشہ عناصر کے خلاف بلا تفریق سخت کارروائیاں جاری رکھی جائیں گی۔

stories.title: India food regulator orders intensified surveillance on packaged water industry
stories.summary:
India's food safety authority has issued a confidential directive to all states demanding stronger regulatory oversight and stricter surveillance of packaged drinking water and mineral water manufacturers. Dated November 25, the order by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India aims to ensure rigorous compliance across the sector.

The regulatory crackdown follows a recent announcement revealing that a sample from Bisleri, the country's leading bottled water brand, was found unsafe due to the presence of potentially cancer-causing chemicals. While Bisleri maintains that its products are safe and that its own testing showed no issues, the regulator has announced plans to initiate court prosecution proceedings against the company.

This intensified scrutiny expands regulatory oversight to major corporations that have heavily invested in India's rapidly growing $3.5 billion packaged water market. Brands operated by PepsiCo, Tata Consumer, Coca-Cola, and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Consumer, alongside high-end natural mineral water brands targeting health-conscious consumers, will face increased checks.

State officials have been instructed to conduct regular inspections and risk-based sampling of bottled water products to enforce safety standards. The move aligns with a broader governmental push for stricter enforcement against major food and beverage brands regarding product quality and labeling compliance.

stories.title: Security forces eliminate 12 militants during intelligence-based operations in Balochistan
stories.summary:
Pakistan security forces killed 12 militants belonging to the group Fitna-al-Hindustan during four separate intelligence-based operations in Balochistan between November 20 and 23. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, the operations were carried out to counter foreign-sponsored terrorism in the region.

The first engagement occurred on November 20 in the Nushki district, where security personnel raided a terrorist hideout and killed eight militants after a heavy exchange of fire, alongside recovering weapons and ammunition. Subsequent operations on November 21 in Sibi and on November 22 and 23 in Panjgur and Kech resulted in the deaths of four additional fighters.

State authorities use the designation Fitna-al-Hindustan for these Balochistan-based groups to underscore India's alleged involvement in fostering terrorism within Pakistan. The military's media wing emphasized that counterterrorism efforts under the Azm-i-Istehkam vision will persist at full speed to eradicate the threat of militant violence.

This security push follows a series of recent counter-militancy sweeps across Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Recent statistical assessments indicate that while the frequency of terror attacks has fluctuated, militant violence and security responses remain a critical focus for the country's defense apparatus.

stories.title: Upcoming European Elections Threaten EU Stability and Decision-Making
stories.summary:
Europe faces an unprecedented series of political tests as four of the European Union's five largest nations prepare to elect new leaders between now and the end of 2027. This electoral cycle is marked by the rise of eurosceptic forces seeking to shift power away from Brussels back to individual member states. These impending contests threaten to trigger political paralysis within the twenty-seven-nation bloc.

The high-stakes sequence begins with an election in Spain, where Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez faces a challenge from conservative opponent Alberto Nunez Feijoo amid debates over housing and immigration. Meanwhile, France prepares for presidential elections in April and May, featuring far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen leading the polls. Le Pen's radical platform includes cutting France's EU budget contribution, downgrading the European Commission to a mere secretariat, and ending aid to Ukraine, placing her on a direct collision course with EU institutions.

Additional contests are scheduled across the continent, including in Italy, Poland, Estonia, Greece, Finland, and Slovakia. These races highlight deep ideological divides regarding relations with Russia, military support for Ukraine, and the overarching vision for European integration. Brussels officials are actively gaming out worst-case scenarios and attempting to safeguard the EU's upcoming seven-year budget and financial support for Ukraine through 2027.

While some diplomats express concern that a victory by eurosceptic leaders could grind EU policymaking to a halt, others suggest that incoming leaders may ultimately be forced to operate within established European frameworks, much like Italy's Giorgia Meloni. Nonetheless, analysts and diplomats agree that the bloc must urgently strengthen its resilience to weather the upcoming wave of political shocks.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Rise Due to Indonesian Export Fee Proposal
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures experienced an increase, driven by a proposed export verification fee in Indonesia that could redirect global buyers toward Malaysia. The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange rose by twenty-six ringgit, representing a zero-point-six-one percent increase to reach four thousand two hundred fifty-five ringgit per metric ton by the midday break.

According to Pelindung Bestari director Paramalingam Supramaniam, the price adjustment follows an announcement regarding Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia, a commodity export monitoring firm established by Indonesia, which proposed a charge of zero-point-five percent on the export sales value of palm oil. Market participants anticipate this charge will encourage buyers to source crude palm oil from Malaysia instead, cementing its status as the world's second-biggest palm oil exporter.

Additional support for the contract came from the Malaysian ringgit, which weakened by zero-point-five percent against the dollar. However, market gains were limited by high ending inventory stocks and sluggish demand. Meanwhile, rival edible oils showed mixed results, with Dalian's soyoil contract slipping zero-point-two percent and its palm oil contract dropping zero-point-sixteen percent.

Industry outlooks from the Malaysian Palm Oil Council suggest that crude palm oil prices will likely remain above four thousand one hundred ringgit per metric ton through December due to anticipated supply risks heading into 2027. Concurrently, independent inspection companies AmSpec Agri Malaysia and Intertek Testing Services reported drops in Malaysian palm oil product exports between November first and twenty-fifth compared to the same period in October.

stories.title: Jannik Sinner Out for Australian Open Following Knee Surgery
stories.summary:
World number two tennis star Jannik Sinner will miss the upcoming Australian Open in January after undergoing surgery for a persistent knee problem. Organizers of the Grand Slam tournament confirmed the absence on Thursday following discussions with the Italian player's management team. Sinner revealed the operation earlier in the week, and Italian sports publication Corriere dello Sport reported that the recovery period could last up to four months. This timeline extends an already lengthy hiatus for the twenty-five-year-old athlete, who has remained away from competitive play since securing his fifth Grand Slam title at Wimbledon in July. Initially, expectations had pointed toward a potential return in time for the Melbourne tournament, which is scheduled to begin on January seventeenth.
Tennis Australia CEO Andrew Abdo stated that tournament organizers have been in regular contact with Sinner's representatives regarding the recent procedure. Abdo expressed support for the player's recovery and noted that Sinner is already looking forward to competing again at the Australian Open in 2028. Sinner previously captured the championship title in Melbourne in both 2024 and 2025.

stories.title: Pakistan and Maldives Target May 2027 for Direct Flight Launch
stories.summary:
Pakistan and the Maldives are aiming to launch direct flights by May 2027 as part of a broader initiative to strengthen bilateral trade, tourism, investment, and shipping connectivity. The timeline was discussed during a meeting in Karachi between Pakistan's Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan and Maldivian Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister Mohamed Saeed, held on the sidelines of FoodAg Pakistan 2026.

The discussions encompassed a comprehensive framework of economic cooperation, including maritime links, healthcare collaboration, and human resource development. The Maldivian delegation, which included the chief executive of the Maldivian national airline, confirmed that May 2027 is the target window for launching direct air services, pending the finalization of necessary arrangements.

Jam Kamal emphasized that sustainable connectivity via direct flights and commercially viable shipping services is vital for building reliable supply chains and boosting bilateral commerce. He highlighted numerous export opportunities for Pakistan, ranging from agricultural goods and pharmaceuticals to textiles and industrial materials, provided they meet Maldivian quality standards. Furthermore, the two sides explored investments in Maldivian tourism, particularly halal tourism and Shariah-compliant resort developments.

Human resource cooperation and medical tourism were also central to the talks, with the Maldivian side pointing to a growing demand for skilled professionals in healthcare and hospitality. Proposals were put forward for Pakistani training institutions to design specialized programs that match the requirements of Maldivian resorts. Additionally, discussions addressed establishing commercial maritime and logistics networks linking Pakistan, the Maldives, and East African markets such as Tanzania, contingent upon maintaining sufficient cargo movement.

stories.title: Pakistan Cellular Imports Jump Over Twenty-Five Percent In October
stories.summary:
Official figures released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics indicate that cellular phone imports in the country rose by 25.21 percent during October, hitting a total of Rs. 50.22 billion. This figure marks a noticeable increase from the previous month, when cellular imports stood at Rs. 39.725 billion. Furthermore, broader telecommunications sector imports experienced a monthly growth of 28.43 percent, climbing from Rs. 60.934 billion in the prior month to reach Rs. 78.273 billion in October. 

In addition to cellular devices, imports associated with mobile phone equipment and accessories saw a sharp monthly surge of 70.88 percent. The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics reported that the value of imported accessories and related equipment exceeded Rs. 28 billion during the month of October alone. 

Looking at the broader fiscal timeline covering the first four months of the 2026 fiscal year, spanning from July through October, cumulative mobile phone imports reached Rs. 166.205 billion. Over this same four-month duration, total imports for the entire telecommunications sector amounted to Rs. 259.33 billion, while accessories and related equipment imports totaled Rs. 93.125 billion.

In a separate development impacting the aviation sector, the Civil Aviation Authority authorized Pakistan International Airlines to utilize planes from Saudi airline operators on a charter basis. According to sources, this arrangement aims to ease passenger transportation between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

stories.title: Military Operations in Balochistan Leave Twelve Terrorists Dead
stories.summary:
Twelve terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan were killed by security forces during a series of intelligence-based operations in Balochistan, the Inter-Services Public Relations announced on Thursday. The counterterrorism missions were carried out across Nushki, Sevi, Panjgur, and Kech districts starting from November 20.

On the first day of operations in Nushki district, security personnel raided a militant hideout. Following a heavy exchange of fire, eight insurgents were neutralized, and security forces seized various weapons and ammunition from the site. The following day, on November 21, troops intercepted moving militants in Sevi district, killing two more.

Further raids were executed on November 22 and 23 in Panjgur and Kech districts, where two additional terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed faction were killed in separate engagements. The military's media wing stated that these actions form part of an ongoing nationwide counterterrorism strategy.

The ISPR emphasized that the operations are being conducted under the vision of "Azm-e-Istehkam," which was approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan. Law enforcement agencies remain fully dedicated to removing the threat of foreign-sponsored terrorism from Pakistan.

stories.title: Fazl Warns of Nationwide Shutdown if JUI-F Convoy Is Blocked
stories.summary:
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman warned of a nationwide shutdown on Thursday if authorities impeded his party's convoy en route to a scheduled public gathering in Sargodha. Speaking to supporters near Thokar Niaz Baig on Multan Road in Lahore, Fazl asserted that his party members were peaceful and disciplined, demanding that the government remove roadblocks and clear their path. He stated that the party was merely exercising its constitutional and democratic right to travel, cautioning that if the convoy was blocked, the entire country would remain shut down. JUI-F Sindh Secretary General Rashid Mahmood Soomro also commented on the situation, remarking that the government had inadvertently transformed a local rally into a nationwide event.

The confrontation followed preemptive administrative actions taken by the Sargodha district administration. On November 25, Sargodha Deputy Commissioner Hussain Ahmad Raza Chaudhary issued a 30-day ban under Section 7(1) of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, barring Fazl and eight other individuals from entering, residing, or remaining within the district. The administration cited police reports alleging that the named individuals routinely made provocative speeches that threatened public safety and law and order. The restricted individuals include Maulana Naseer Ahmad Abrar, Maulana Amjad Khan, Maulana Safi Ullah, Prof Ghazanfar Aziz, Maulana Muhammad Noor Khan Hans, Maulana Muhammad Zakria Shah, Maulana Muhammad Yahya Abbasi, and Maulana Jamal Abdul Nasir. Additionally, the administration enforced a 30-day gag order on 19 other local figures and religious scholars to prevent speech-related disturbances.

In response to the travel restrictions and government resistance, JUI-F supporters staged sit-ins and blocked major roads and highways across various cities, including Karachi, Kohistan, Chitral, Chaman, and Makran. Fazl maintained that his party's political history is rooted in peaceful struggle and emphasized that despite administrative oppression, their resolve would remain unbroken as the standoff continued.

stories.title: Karachi Police Register Sealed FIR After Deadly Building Collapse
stories.summary:
Karachi police registered a criminal case at the Tipu Sultan Police Station on behalf of the state following a fatal building collapse in the Admin Society.
